jobs.excerpt: Why Mozilla? Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years.
jobs.description:
Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About this team and role

Mozilla is seeking experienced browser engineers to join a small team exploring new applications of browser technology. The work combines deep systems engineering, rapid experimentation, and close collaboration across technical disciplines.

We are looking for a browser engine specialist who enjoys turning difficult systems questions into working experiments. You will investigate browser behavior, implement changes deep in the engine, and establish which ideas produce meaningful improvements. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with ownership of engine-level investigations and implementation, working closely with the team’s technical lead.

The work suits someone who has built or substantially changed browser internals, understands the tradeoffs embedded in those systems, and enjoys applying that knowledge to unfamiliar problems. Your experiments will help inform technical direction.

What you'll do:

Design and implement experiments within browser engine subsystems. Investigate how internal data structures and execution behavior affect performance, correctness, and the interfaces exposed to developer tools.

Evaluate ways to represent and expose browser state efficiently and accurately. Identify the tradeoffs in each approach, including information loss, implementation complexity, and compatibility with dynamic web content.

Prototype engine capabilities that support reliable programmatic interaction with web content. Investigate how document structure, layout, navigation, and event handling affect correctness and performance.

Instrument browser behavior and evaluate changes against repeatable tasks. Measure performance and correctness, isolate the effect of each change, and document unsuccessful experiments as clearly as successful ones. Check that gains hold beyond the workloads used to develop the prototype.

Profile the overhead introduced by new capabilities and pursue improvements where measurements justify them. Use AI tools to accelerate coding and analysis, and verify their output through debugging, tests, and measurement.

What you'll bring:

  • Deep hands-on expertise in at least one browser engine subsystem, such as DOM and Web APIs, layout and rendering, accessibility, JavaScript runtimes, or networking and process architecture. You have implemented substantial changes and can trace their effects into neighboring subsystems.
  • Strong proficiency in C++ or Rust, experience navigating a large systems codebase, and practical knowledge of memory ownership, concurrency, object lifetimes, and performance debugging. You can build the JavaScript and scripting tools needed to exercise and measure your work.
  • A demonstrated ability to investigate unfamiliar code, form a precise hypothesis, construct a useful prototype, and interpret the results. You can separate the effects of your implementation from variability in websites, workloads, or model behavior.
  • A strong understanding of web platform behavior and compatibility. You can reason about how document structure, script execution, rendering, and user interaction relate, including cases where the browser’s internal state is difficult to expose accurately to another system.
  • Experience with profiling, tracing, regression tests, or conformance tests, and a habit of grounding performance claims in reproducible evidence. You can explain both the benefit of an optimization and the circumstances in which it fails.
  • Curiosity about AI agents and a willingness to work directly with agent harnesses and coding tools. You can connect a low-level implementation choice to the information an agent receives and the work it must do next.

Nice to have:

  • Contributions to Gecko, Servo, Blink, WebKit, or another browser engine
  • Experience maintaining an open-source project
  • Technical leadership in a small team building a new product
  • Experience with accessibility infrastructure, browser security, profiling, or automated evaluation of agent workflows

What you’ll get:

  • Generous performance-based bonus plans to all eligible employees - we share in our success as one team
  • Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute)
  • Quarterly all-company wellness days where everyone takes a pause together
  • Country specific holidays plus a day off for your birthday
  • One-time home office stipend
  • Annual professional development budget
  • Quarterly well-being stipend
  • Considerable paid parental leave
  • Employee referral bonus program
  • Other benefits (life/AD&D, disability, EAP, etc. - varies by country)

About Mozilla

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Join us to work on the Web as the platform and help create more opportunity and innovation for everyone online.

Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging

Mozilla understands that valuing diverse creative practices and forms of knowledge are crucial to and enrich the company’s core mission. We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, persons of all sexual orientations, gender identities, and expressions.

jobs.description:
Remote-based in the US

Overview

GoodPower is a global organization working to unlock the economic potential of decarbonization through research, innovation, strategic communications, and disruptive technology. We focus on advancing more affordable and reliable energy, expanding economic opportunity, strengthening energy security, supporting healthier and more resilient communities, and accelerating the transition to a predictable, secure, modern low-carbon economy.

Operating at the intersection of data, digital media, emerging technology, behavioral research, and public engagement, GoodPower develops and deploys scalable strategies designed to accelerate the adoption of decarbonized technologies and infrastructure—including renewable energy, regenerative agriculture, energy storage, and electric transportation. Our work combines rigorous research and experimentation with advanced communications and innovation capabilities to better understand public attitudes, test effective interventions, and help build the social, economic, and market conditions necessary for large-scale transformation.

GoodPower is at a pivotal stage of organizational growth as we approach completion of the first year of our 2030 Strategic Plan. Over the next five years, we intend to significantly expand our reach, capabilities, and impact—investing deeply in innovation, AI-enabled systems, data and analytics, research and development, and next-generation communications infrastructure to help accelerate the global energy transition and the economic opportunities it creates.

Job Summary

The Content Creator’s primary role will be to provide social-first video production across GoodPower and its affiliated brands and partners, with a focus on producing mobile-first content for TikTok, Instagram, YouTube Shorts and paid media. The Content Creator is a resourceful, trend-aware creative professional with a versatile skillset, a natural and engaging on-camera presence, sharp editing skills and a dedication to GoodPower’s mission to advance a zero-carbon economy. They will collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to produce timely, platform-specific content that is brand aligned, visually engaging and compelling.

In this position, the Content Creator will support and execute all phases of the short-form content production process, including concept development, scripting, filming, on-camera hosting, editing and platform-ready delivery for GoodPower and its affiliated entities, social media channels and online media campaigns. The Content Creator brings strong creative instincts and the ability to move quickly from concept to finished product, while producing both planned and rapid response content. This role will focus on translating GoodPower’s research, campaigns and narrative priorities into accessible, social-first content that reflects platform-specific best practices, internet culture, creator trends and audience behavior.

While this position will focus primarily on short-form video and social content, the Content Creator will also support basic social creative needs including Instagram carousels, static memes and Canva-based assets as needs and capacity shift based on priorities. The Content Creator reports to the Senior Director of Video on the Agency team.

This is a full-time position based anywhere in the United States. The Content Creator will work from home, meet as required by video chat with teams, and have weekly national full staff meetings with colleagues online. Some domestic travel may be required for content capture, relevant events, staff retreats and other convenings as needed.

Key Responsibilities

Video Production:

  • Own short-form, mobile-first video production end to end, including concept development, scripting, on-camera hosting, filming, editing and platform-ready delivery for TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and paid media

  • Translate complex issues related to affordability, clean energy, jobs and economic opportunity into clear and engaging social content

  • Create content that reflects platform-specific best practices, including pacing, visual storytelling and audience behavior

  • Support creative experimentation by testing new formats, platform features, creator trends and rapid-turn concepts

  • Help steward GoodPower’s brand voice across creator-led and social-first content

  • Produce basic social media creative, including Instagram carousels, static memes and Canva-based assets

  • Manage multiple video projects simultaneously, including rapid response production and turnaround, ensuring timely delivery, adherence to project requirements and high-quality output

Collaborative Projects:

  • Collaborate closely with Agency and Social teams, outside vendors and across teams to ensure project success

  • Communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders, including team leads to understand priorities and needs to deliver exceptional content

Other Responsibilities:

  • Contribute to the continuous improvement and implementation of our content processes and workflows to increase speed, efficiency and scalability

  • Perform other content production-related tasks as needed to support GoodPower and its partners

  • Adapt to the evolving needs of a fast-paced organization with flexibility and creativity

Qualifications

Experience & Skills

  • 3–5 years of experience creating and starring in social content for a brand, nonprofit, agency, campaign, creator business or personal channel, with a portfolio showing strong short-form video production, editing and on-camera presence

  • Proven ability to independently concept, script, shoot and edit social video content

  • Strong mobile-first video editing skills (Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro X, CapCut, InShot or similar)

  • Natural, confident on-camera presence, with the range to shift between clear explanation, storytelling and entertainment-driven content

  • Strong grasp of hooks, pacing, visual storytelling and platform-specific best practices across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube Shorts and emerging platforms

  • Deep familiarity with internet culture, creator trends, memes and short-form formats

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, plus solid general computer skills (Google Apps, etc.)

Attributes

  • Strong creative judgment — brings ideas, not just edits

  • Self-starter with strong organizational skills, comfortable juggling multiple projects and moving between planned content calendars and rapid-response needs while maintaining attention to detail

  • Collaborative team player who also works well independently, communicates across teams, and is eager to pitch in beyond assigned duties

  • Proactive, flexible and solutions-oriented, with a commitment to innovation and to fostering a culture of excellence, quality and inclusivity

  • Open to constructive feedback and skilled at finding solutions to notes or critiques

Desired Qualifications:

  • Experience creating content for advocacy, political, nonprofit, clean energy or issue-based campaigns

  • Experience using Canva or similar tools to create social graphics, carousels, memes or other lightweight creative assets

  • Experience producing rapid response content tied to news, platform trends or campaign moments

  • Comfort interpreting research, policy or campaign messaging and turning it into clear, accessible social content

  • Existing expertise in the climate, renewable energy and democracy spaces

  • Experience leveraging AI tools to support content production, scripting, research, ideation, editing workflows or creative experimentation, or a willingness to learn and integrate AI tools into the production process

Job Summary

Compensation, Benefits, and Perks

  • Annual salary range: $80,000-87,000, commensurate with experience

  • Perform a line-by-line quality check before submitting work to reduce errors and omissions.

Experience & Skills Required

  • Advanced Microsoft Word skills, especially formatting (tables, tabs, spacing, page layout, headers/footers, styles).
  • Excellent attention to detail and comfort with doing meticulous, repetitive work.

jobs.excerpt: Elior Support Services – The People Behind Every Plate Every great meal starts somewhere.
jobs.description:
Elior Support Services – The People Behind Every Plate Every great meal starts somewhere. Not just in our kitchens, but in the teams that support them.

Whether you're driving strategy, managing risk, building brands, supporting our people, or keeping our business running smoothly, your work helps create the conditions for great food and exceptional service. You may not be on the frontline. But your influence will be felt in every dish served, every contract won and every guest experience we create.

We’re looking for a Business Development Manager to join our team and play a key role in growing Elior’s business across the UK. This is a role for a genuine sales professional who knows how to spot an opportunity, build a compelling proposition and turn a first conversation into a signed contract. You’ll own your business development pipeline, seek out new tender opportunities and lead the sales journey from those all-important first conversations through to closing the deal. You’ll work closely with our Operations, Marketing, Finance and Legal teams to create commercially strong, creative and compelling solutions that show clients exactly why Elior is the right partner for them. And you won’t simply hand a contract over once it’s won. You’ll remain involved through mobilisation and key retention activity, helping ensure the client experience lives up to the promise made during the sales process. This is a home-based role, with equipment provided, so you can be based anywhere in the UK. You’ll need a full UK driving licence and be comfortable travelling to meet clients and attend key business meetings. If you’re commercially sharp, naturally curious, confident in front of clients and motivated by the thrill of winning new business, we want to hear from you. What you’ll be serving up…

  • Building your own pipeline, actively researching the market, networking and identifying new business and tender opportunities across the UK.
  • Creating opportunities, developing relationships with prospective clients and positioning Elior as a credible, innovative and compelling catering partner.
  • Owning the sales process, from initial contact and discovery meetings through to solution development, presentations, negotiation and contract close.
  • Leading winning tenders, bringing together the right people across Operations, Finance, Marketing and Legal to develop solutions that are commercially viable and genuinely meet the client’s needs.
  • Selling the Elior proposition, confidently communicating our USPs and tailoring our story to what matters most to each client.
  • Using your commercial instinct, understanding the opportunity, the competition, the numbers and what it will take to turn a prospect into a profitable contract.
  • Building strong client relationships, taking the time to understand their challenges and becoming someone they want to do business with.
  • Bringing creativity to your solutions, working with internal teams to develop compelling written proposals, presentations and service solutions.
  • Keeping the momentum, managing multiple opportunities and deadlines simultaneously while ensuring every prospect receives a high-quality and professional experience.
  • Supporting successful mobilisation, staying connected after the win to help ensure the transition from signed contract to operational delivery is seamless.
  • Supporting key retention activity, coordinating bids, presentations and commercial activity where existing contracts are up for renewal.
  • Taking ownership of your numbers, managing your weekly activity, maintaining accurate pipeline information and reporting progress against your sales targets.

The ingredients you’ll bring…

  • Proven experience in business development, sales or contract acquisition, ideally within contract catering or food service.
  • A strong understanding of the UK contract catering market and what it takes to win new business.
  • A proven track record of securing new contracts, ideally including experience across food service and/or healthcare.
  • Strong commercial acumen, with the confidence to understand the numbers, challenge assumptions and negotiate effectively.
  • Excellent relationship-building skills. You’ll be comfortable developing relationships from first contact through to senior-level client conversations.
  • Confidence leading tenders, presentations and sales meetings, with the ability to influence and engage a range of stakeholders.
  • Strong writing skills and the creativity to turn a brief into a compelling commercial solution.
  • Experience managing multiple tenders and opportunities simultaneously, with exceptional organisation and the ability to meet tight deadlines.
  • The ability to collaborate effectively with Operations, Finance, Marketing, Legal and other specialist teams to develop winning bids.
  • Excellent communication, listening and interpersonal skills, with the ability to understand what a client really needs rather than simply selling a standard solution.
  • Strong IT skills and confidence working with CRM, tendering and sales tools.
  • A full UK driving licence and willingness to travel as required.

What really matters We’re looking for someone who is hungry to win. Someone who doesn’t wait for opportunities to land in their inbox, but gets out there, builds relationships, asks the right questions and creates opportunities. You’ll need the commercial confidence to challenge, the creativity to develop a proposition that stands out and the resilience to keep going when a deal doesn’t go your way. Most importantly, you’ll understand that great business development isn’t just about winning the contract. It’s about winning the right contract, building the right relationships and creating sustainable growth for Elior.

What's on the menu for you… At Elior, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported, valued and able to thrive. That's why we offer a benefits package designed to support your wellbeing, career, finances and life outside of work. Here’s a taste of what you can expect when you join us:

  • Free lunches provided
  • Flexible and part-time working opportunities
  • Company car or car allowance
  • Private Healthcare
  • 33 days holiday, with the option to buy up to an additional 10 days per year
  • Rewarding bonus package up to 15%
  • Enhanced family, personal and compassionate leave policies
  • Paid volunteering days
  • Training, development and career progression opportunities
  • Pension scheme, life assurance and financial wellbeing support
  • Salary Advance, giving you access to a portion of your pay before payday
  • A supportive, inclusive culture where everyone can thrive

Plus access to Elior Spark, our enhanced wellbeing platform, offering support for you and your immediate family, including:

  • 24/7 virtual GP appointments
  • Mental health support, counselling and therapy sessions
  • Physiotherapy services and second medical opinions
  • Online gym and workout programmes
  • Legal and financial advice
  • Nutrition, fitness and lifestyle guidance
  • Meditation and mindfulness resources
  • Dedicated wellbeing helplines and expert support whenever you need it

Fancy being part of the recipe? At Elior, over 10,000 colleagues come together every day with one purpose: to enrich lives everywhere, every day. We're proud that 87% of our colleagues are proud to work here — and we think that's because people are given the support, trust and opportunities they need to thrive. Don't tick every box? Don't rule yourself out. We're looking for people with potential, passion and the right attitude, not just a checklist of experience. We're committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels they belong. If you need any adjustments during the recruitment process, just let us know.

Ready to join us? Hit ‘Apply Now’ and let’s chat!

Job Description:

GDIT is looking for a Senior Technical Solutions Manager to own the delivery posture across our entire U.S. Courts portfolio — currently four active call orders under the Case Management Modernization (CMM) program for the Administrative Office of the United States Courts (AOUSC). This is not a single-workstream PM role. The Senior Technical Solutions Manager will see across all four call orders, connect the dependencies between them, identify gaps and risks before they surface, and drive the program toward its contractual commitments.


The CMM program is replacing the federal courts’ 30-year-old case management system (CM/ECF) with a cloud-native, multi-tenant SaaS platform serving all 204 federal courts. It is a multi-vendor, SAFe-structured environment with parallel workstreams, government-controlled dependencies, and high stakeholder visibility. The ideal candidate thrives complexity and exercises sound judgment in escalations and resolutions.


What You’ll Do

  • Own cross-call-order visibility. Maintain a unified view of schedule, risk, dependencies, and delivery status across all four call orders
  • Drive risk and dependency management
  • Identify cross-program risks and inter-team dependencies early, track them rigorously, and drive resolution
  • Run program-level status and governance
  • Own the cadence: PI planning readiness, sprint-level health, milestone tracking, executive reporting
  • Build the operating rhythm that keeps four parallel workstreams synchronized
  • Ensure contractual alignment and flag gaps before they become findings
  • Manage stakeholder communication and serve as the primary program interface for internal leadership and coordinate with government stakeholders.
  • Translate technical execution status into business-level impact for both audiences.
  • Coordinate across vendors and teams
  • Work across GDIT delivery teams, the cloud/DevSecOps contractor, and the advisory contractor to ensure dependencies are tracked and ensure handoffs
  • Support capture and option year planning
  • Provide the execution data and program health visibility

What You Bring

Required

  • 10+ years of technical program management experience, with at least 5 years managing multiple concurrent workstreams or contracts
  • Demonstrated experience in government contracting or heavily regulated environments (understanding PWS/SOW obligations, CDRLs, option year mechanics, and contractual performance standards)
  • Hands-on risk and dependency management — not just maintaining a register, but actively driving resolution and escalating with judgment
  • Experience operating in multi-vendor delivery environments where you don’t control all the teams but are accountable for the integrated outcome
  • Proficiency with Agile/SAFe delivery frameworks at scale (PI planning, sprint cadences, cross-team synchronization across 5+ teams)
  • Strong executive communication, both written and verbal
  • Ability to obtain a Public Trust clearance

Preferred

  • Experience with Judiciary, DOJ, or court administration programs
  • Familiarity with cloud-native modernization programs (legacy-to-cloud migrations, microservices, API-first architectures)
  • PMP, PgMP, SAFe SPC, or equivalent certifications
  • Experience with JIRA, GitLab, or similar delivery management tooling at portfolio level
  • Background in case management, document management, or records management systems

Clearance & Compliance

This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust determination. Work is performed in compliance with JISF (Judiciary Information Security Framework) and FedRAMP High requirements.

Location & Work Model

This is a remote position. Occasional travel to Washington, D.C. or other AOUSC/GDIT locations may be required for PI planning events, program reviews, or stakeholder meetings (estimated 10–15% travel).

About the Team

GDIT’s Courts portfolio supports the Administrative Office of the United States Courts in modernizing the technology that serves all 204 federal courts. The CMM program is one of the largest modernization initiatives in the Judiciary — replacing a system that has been in use for over two decades and touches 60 million cases, 1.5 billion docket entries, and 5+ million users. You’ll work alongside delivery teams, architects, product owners, and government stakeholders who are building something that will fundamentally change how the federal courts operate. This is visible, complex, high-stakes work — and the right person will see that as exactly why they want the job.

The likely salary range for this position is $187,179 - $224,250. This is not, however, a guarantee of compensation or salary. Rather, salary will be set based on experience, geographic location and possibly contractual requirements and could fall outside of this range.

Total Rewards at GDIT:

Our benefits package for all US-based employees includes a variety of medical plan options, some with Health Savings Accounts, dental plan options, a vision plan, and a 401(k) plan offering the ability to contribute both pre and post-tax dollars up to the IRS annual limits and receive a company match. To encourage work/life balance, GDIT offers employees full flex work weeks where possible and a variety of paid time off plans, including vacation, sick and personal time, holidays, paid parental, military, bereavement and jury duty leave. GDIT typically provides new employees with 15 days of paid leave per calendar year to be used for vacations, personal business, and illness and an additional 10 paid holidays per year. Paid leave and paid holidays are prorated based on the employee’s date of hire. The GDIT Paid Family Leave program provides a total of up to 160 hours of paid leave in a rolling 12 month period for eligible employees. To ensure our employees are able to protect their income, other offerings such as short and long-term disability benefits, life, accidental death and dismemberment, personal accident, critical illness and business travel and accident insurance are provided or available. We regularly review our Total Rewards package to ensure our offerings are competitive and reflect what our employees have told us they value most.

Our Identity Verification Process:

As part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during virtual interviews. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud. By proceeding, you authorize the collection, processing, and use of your biometric data for identity verification and security purposes.

We are GDIT. A global technology and professional services company that delivers technology solutions and mission services to every major agency across the U.S. government, defense and intelligence community. Our 26,000 experts extract the power of technology to create immediate value and deliver solutions at the edge of innovation. jobs.description:
Medical Virtual Assistant (MVA)

Remote | Chiropractic Clinic | 30 Hours/Week | $5-$6/hour
performance-based increase after 6 months

Position Overview

We are seeking a highly capable Medical Virtual Assistant (MVA) to support the overall operational health of a busy healthcare clinic. This role is ideal for someone who is very sharp, proactive, detail-oriented, emotionally intelligent, and able to take ownership of important clinic workflows with minimal supervision.

This is not a basic task-following role. The ideal candidate must be able to think ahead, identify operational gaps, take initiative, and help remove administrative and billing-related tasks from the provider's plate.

We are looking for someone with excellent English communication skills, strong executive presence, high accountability, and the ability to build a trust-based working relationship with the provider and care team.

Key Responsibilities

Insurance Verification

Verify patient insurance after the patient checks in, typically around 15 minutes after the scheduled appointment time. Ensure all insurance information is accurate, updated, and properly documented.

Denied Claims Management

Review denied claims, identify denial reasons, and assist with claim reprocessing. Track issues, follow up on missing information, and help prevent repeat claim errors.

EOB Processing

Review and process Explanation of Benefits documents. Help organize, validate, and clear EOB backlogs while ensuring billing and insurance documentation is accurate.

Patient Balance Resolution

Review outstanding insurance balances and patient account issues. Track unresolved balances, identify the source of the issue, and coordinate next steps for resolution.

Claims Processing

Support claims-related workflows, including Cigna and Veterans Affairs claims. Ensure claims are reviewed, tracked, and escalated when necessary.

Payment Coordination

Assist with vendor payment coordination, including check payments when needed. Ensure payment-related tasks are completed accurately and on time.

SOAP Note Monitoring

Monitor SOAP note completion, accuracy, and compliance. Track missing, incomplete, or delayed documentation and communicate concerns appropriately.

Appointment Tracking

Track missed appointments, canceled appointments, and scheduling trends. Identify patterns that may affect clinic revenue, patient flow, or provider productivity.

Reports and Operational Tracking

Prepare reports on outstanding balances, missed appointments, canceled appointments, EOB backlog, denied claims, and other operational metrics. Reports should include clear insights and practical recommendations when needed.

Team Coordination

Support smooth communication between the provider, care team, and administrative staff. Help ensure updates are clearly shared, priorities are followed through, and important tasks are not missed.

Operational Support

Proactively identify workflow gaps, billing concerns, documentation delays, scheduling issues, and patient account problems. Recommend practical solutions to improve clinic efficiency.

Mandatory Requirements

  • Minimum of 1 year of experience as a Medical Virtual Assistant

  • Experience supporting a US healthcare practice

  • Experience with insurance verification, EOBs, claims, denied claims, patient balances, or billing support

  • Exposure to CPT and ICD-10 codes

  • Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal

  • Strong executive presence and professional communication style

  • Must be a Mac OS user

  • Strong attention to detail and follow-through

  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision

  • Proven leadership, ownership, or high-accountability experience in a previous role

Required Soft Skills

  • Proactive and able to anticipate needs before being asked

  • Highly detail-oriented with billing, documentation, and reporting tasks

  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills

  • Emotionally intelligent and patient when working with a busy provider

  • Confident, professional, and organized in communication

  • Able to take personal responsibility for assigned work

  • Resourceful and self-motivated when learning new workflows

  • Trustworthy, dependable, and comfortable handling sensitive information

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience supporting a chiropractic clinic

  • Experience with Cigna or Veterans Affairs claims

  • Experience clearing EOB or billing backlogs

  • Experience preparing operational or billing reports

  • Experience mentoring, training, or supporting new team members

  • Experience working closely with a clinic owner, provider, or executive-level leader

Schedule and Compensation

  • Schedule: Monday to Friday

  • Hours: 6 hours per day, 30 hours per week

  • Rate: $6 per hour

  • Work Setup: Remote

  • Device Requirement: Mac OS required

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is someone who does not wait to be told every step. This person should be observant, organized, and confident enough to identify what needs attention.

They should be able to manage detailed billing and administrative tasks while also thinking about the bigger picture of clinic operations. The right candidate will be sharp, emotionally intelligent, highly reliable, and capable of becoming a trusted operational support partner for the provider and care team.

jobs.description:
Full Time - 1 year term (with possibility for extension)

Closing Dates:

  • Nigeria & India - Closing date: 4th November
  • Kenya & Pakistan - Recruitment has closed. Please be aware are unable to consider applications received from individuals in Kenya & Pakistan after 5pm BST on 7th Oct.

Location: Remote (timezone: UTC -1 to UTC +5). Country specific locations: Nigeria, India, Kenya, & Pakistan.
Compensation: Peek benchmarks annual salary based on market ranges per jurisdiction. To learn the hiring ranges for this position, please review the Application Instructions below.

The Role

Division: Delivery

Team: Training & Support; Meet the Peek Team
Travel: up to 40% travel per annum
Working Day: Flexible working hours throughout the week. Daily collective overlapping hours are 11:00-16:00 UTC. Our Full Time work week is approximately 40 hours.

Sitting within the Training & Support team and reporting to the Head of Partner Enablement, the Partner Enablement Lead enables implementing partners and software users in low and middle-income countries to adopt Peek's software and data intelligence platform confidently, use it correctly, and keep improving how they use it over time. This is a coaching and facilitation role where success is measured by partner adoption and confident, independent use of Peek software to train non-eye health professionals (screeners) with quality outcomes.

The role transfers knowledge of Peek’s software use and integration into partner eye health programmes where structured learning is delivered through Peek's reusable learning assets (digital/non-digital). The Partner Enablement Lead will facilitate that learning, coach the partner's own trainers to cascade it, quality-assure the cascade, then monitor and intervene where practice, data quality or programme outcomes are impacted.

Peek’s staff are distributed internationally around the globe and our customers and software users operate and deliver programmes in multiple countries. Travel to programmes using Peek in different countries will be part of the role (in line with Peek’s Travel Safety Policy).

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead structured onboarding, enablement and in-country Software User Training (SUT) with Peek’s implementing partners using standard learning assets (digital and non-digital). Deliver demonstrations and facilitative hands-on sessions where they add value beyond self-serve learning.
  • Support field monitoring visits and facilitate software release alignment with partners ensure they keep up to date with Peek’s latest releases
  • Stay up to date with internal software knowledge as Peek’s product evolves
  • Train new Peek staff on Peek Capture and Admin
  • Coach and develop core teams, Trainer of Trainers (ToT) lead trainers, Partner-as-Trainer (PaT) representatives and Training Consultants so Peek training is cascaded confidently and independently
  • Quality assure all Peek training models (ToT, PaT and subsequent cascade models) from Peek through partners’ trainers to end users, using on the ground observation and remote monitoring against the certification framework’s QA criteria. Coach and give feedback where quality falls short, confirming improvement with data informed decision making. Own the assurance and sign-off your core team SUT certification decision, where readiness depends on cascade quality and programme screening outputs.
  • Through remote monitoring, reinforce screening and referral protocols and govern quality of practice, catching issues early and intervening with core teams where necessary. Align quality assurance (QA) activity to team and organisational OKRs, feeding findings and trends into quarterly reporting
  • Attend in-country programme design workshops, leading on configuration. Translate agreed designs into accurate configuration with country Programme Management Leads (PMLs) and partners, following best practice and supporting clean data reporting. Challenge requests that compromise data integrity, finding compliant alternatives with PMLs, partners, Data Insights, Product and Peek’s Software Application Support Engineer. Validate and test workflows with Programme Managers (PMs), IT leads and partner stakeholders before SUT training, ensuring users understand the operational flow created
  • Own software adoption and behaviour-change outcomes so partners use the software confidently, correctly and independently. Monitor usage and engagement alongside outcome data e.g. referral outcomes, false positive rates, screening practices, connected to care rates distinguishing adoption issues from protocol, capability or operational causes. Report programme level outcomes against OKRs working with the Partner Enablement team and Data Insights team to test interpretations. Intervene proactively through coaching, corrective input, protocol reinforcement, configuration review or escalation, and follow up with partners accordingly
  • Act as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) working with the wider enablement team reviewing materials for accuracy and field deliverability so Peek training assets keep improving. Gather partners feedback systematically and channel recurring themes into learning assets, configurations standards or product change working with respective Peek teams
  • Own and triage incoming partner queries, tickets, bugs and enhancement requests, resolving at first line support within agreed SLAs and keeping partners updated. Escalate where needed to the Application Support Engineer and Product Development team with clear reproduction detail, impact and urgency.
  • Plan and manage multiple country team programmes in parallel alongside internal projects with a realistic view of your capacity and flagging conflicts early to the Head of Partner Enablement.
  • Maintain enablement plans covering scope, timelines, dependencies, time spent and owners using Monday.com boards. Keep internal and external meeting notes current and transparent to Peek teams. Prioritise against OKRs, deliver to agreed timelines and flag risks and dependencies in good time.
  • Take full ownership and accountability for your workload, decisions and outcomes. Success in the role is dependent on whether partners achieve programme outcomes and how enablement gaps are closed.
  • Support colleagues toward shared team goals through knowledge sharing, work cover and peer reviews building strong relationships across functions and geographies.
  • Grow your networks at industry events representing Peek and working with our Communications teams to ensure clear messaging and branding of Peek with existing and potential partners\

Key Attributes

  • A teaching or training qualification, with a minimum of 2 years experience as a teacher, trainer or facilitator
  • Demonstrable experience training teams (remotely) in low-middle income countries (LMICs)
  • Strong understanding of software products, software configuration and how customer adoption works in practice
  • Demonstrable experience managing customers or partner relationships, effectively managing expectations and
  • driving programmes to better outcomes
  • Strong coaching and facilitation skills, building capability in others so knowledge sticks. Confident observing
  • practice, giving developmental feedback and holding a quality standards with people you don’t manage
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, explaining technical concepts to non-technical audiences, adapting to varying literacy, digital literacy, English proficiency and cultural context. Credible in front of a room or on a call when working with partners remotely.
  • Confident with data, tracking engagement and outcomes, reaching sound conclusions and translating them into the correct interventions
  • Excellent time and programme management skills
  • High personal ownership and accountability where you are self-directed, reliable and able to thrive in a self-managed environment
  • A collaborative, team first approach that actively supports colleagues to achieve shared goals
  • A scalability mindset, comfortable with change

Desirable Attributes

  • An eye health or clinical background (e.g optometry) or understanding of screening and referral pathways is desirable but not essential
  • Customer success, customer enablement or technical account management experience in a software organisation
  • Experience of Train-the-Trainer (ToT) or other cascade models including QA of delivery in LMICs
  • Experience configuring software for operational and clinical workflows
  • Familiar with learning through digital platforms e.g. LMS or in app
  • Additional language skills relevant to Peek’s partner geographies

About Peek

Millions of people worldwide are losing their sight unnecessarily. We are intent on changing this. Join a mission-driven award winning team who are intent on changing this.

  • Vision and eye health for all - Why Peek exists and the problem we solve
  • What is Peek? - How our product works
  • Kiyasi’s Story - A short film about some of the people who use and benefit from our tools
  • WIRED - How Peek Vision Helped 1.5 Million People to See Again
  • Rolex Perpetual Planet Initiative - Andrew Bastawrous: Global Vision
  • Peek team members often say that working here is more than just a job — it's a chance to make a real impact alongside supportive, mission-driven colleagues.

More than one in eight people worldwide can’t see clearly. By 2050, the number of people affected is expected to double. There aren’t enough eye health specialists to treat everyone, and at the same time many people are invisible to eye health services or never make it to care.

Peek Vision is a social enterprise that exists to help eye care services reach everyone who needs them.

Our software and data insights platform helps to optimise and evaluate eye health services working in schools, communities and workplaces.

Peek supports eye health from planning through to screening and treatment with:

  • Population-level rapid assessments
  • App-based vision screening
  • Data capture and referrals
  • Real-time service monitoring and insights

By 2050, we aim to prevent 1.25 billion people from needlessly losing their eyesight.

We are dynamic, impact-driven and award-winning. Our products have been developed in collaboration with eye health providers, professional bodies and researchers. They reflect global best practices in health systems decision-making.

Peek is powering eye health programmes in multiple countries. One person is screened with Peek every four seconds.

Why work at Peek?

Our team is united around one goal: vision and eye health for all. Your work will have tangible impact, creating lasting improvements in eye health worldwide.

We are a team like no other - our diverse, multidisciplinary team is recruited from a wide range of backgrounds, including technology development, public health, research, eye health, international development and the private sector. Peek promotes a high level of ownership and accountability within each role, with frequent collaboration between team members and across teams. Peek’s culture promotes individual ownership, accountability and collaboration across and within teams, with team leads playing a supportive role in wellbeing, development and prioritisation.

Working for Peek Vision provides a number of benefits - to find out more about our approach to compensation and benefit provision, please visit our Why work at Peek? page on our website.

Application Information & Instructions

To Apply: Please submit your full application through our recruitment site by the closing date noted above.

Salary Ranges: Peek benchmarks annual salary based on market ranges per jurisdiction. A selection of our salary ranges for this role are as follows:

  • 1,890,000 - 2,225,000 INR per annum, based on India jurisdiction
  • 11,000,000 - 13,400,000 NGN per annum, based on Nigeria jurisdiction
  • 3,418,000 - 4,020,000 PKR per annum, based on Pakistan jurisdiction
  • 3,288,000 - 3,868,000 KES per annum, based on Kenya jurisdiction

Please include your salary expectations with your application, regardless of your location. The salary ranges above are provided for selected jurisdictions only. Where a range isn't published for your jurisdiction, we'll discuss the local benchmark and compensation with you during the recruitment process.

Recruitment Processes: Please be aware we may use AI tools to support parts of our recruitment process. All applications are reviewed by our recruitment team, and all decisions about shortlisting and hiring are made by people. AI supports our process but does not make employment decisions.

jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Calibrate is on a mission to change the way the world treats weight by redefining obesity care as a matter of biology, not willpower. Designed by world leaders in metabolic health, our program combines clinical research, personalized coaching, and lifestyle intervention to deliver lasting weight loss and improved metabolic outcomes. With obesity as America’s largest chronic condition, impacting 175mm adults in a $600B market, we’re closing the care gap by offering the first value-based model in obesity treatment.

Since launching Direct-to-Consumer in 2020, we’ve expanded into Enterprise channels to improve access, and our app-based experience supports members with coaching, tailored education, daily tracking, and community engagement across the four pillars of metabolic health: food, sleep, exercise, and emotional wellbeing.

ABOUT THE ROLE

At Calibrate, our clinical team of nurse practitioners, nurses and doctors are at the heart of our mission to change the way the world treats weight by offering comprehensive obesity care that results in life-changing, sustainable results. In this role, you’ll play a pivotal part in delivering evidence-based, patient-centered care that integrates coaching and curriculum for lifestyle support.

We’re looking for nurse practitioners who are passionate about improving lives through a holistic approach to weight health. You'll collaborate with an interdisciplinary team, contribute to an innovative care model, and help patients achieve meaningful, lasting results.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing team and help shape the future of obesity medicine through telehealth. This role offers a chance to make a significant impact in the lives of patients while working in a supportive environment as a seasonal employee working a minimum of 10 hours per week from January 2027 through April 2027.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Consistently provide a world-class level of clinical care and patient experience
  • Review patient intake and provide the initial patient interaction, including the discussion of the scientific principles of obesity and the prescription of appropriate weight loss therapy based on Calibrate clinical protocols
  • Utilize and support a detailed clinical treatment paradigm, developed and updated by the Calibrate team and specialized to support obese patients achieve weight-loss goals
  • Able to commit to at least 10 hours per week in a telehealth (remote) setting with option for up to full-time if interested
  • Follow state regulations for collaboration agreements with supervising physicians as required by each state you’re licensed to practice
  • Applicants must be available to work shifts scheduled between 8:00 am and 10 pm EST and provide a minimum of 10 hours of availability per week (up to 40 hours)

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Board-certified Nurse Practitioner (FNP, AGNP, or other relevant specialties)
  • Active, unrestricted license in AK, AZ, CA, CO, HI, ID, KS, NV, NM, OK, OR, TX, UT, WA (MUST be license in CA or TX)
  • Demonstrated excellent written/verbal communication skills and virtual “bedside” manner

IDEAL QUALITIES

  • A clinical style that will work well with our belief that healthy, long-term, sustainable weight-loss is impossible to achieve without dedicated medical and coaching support
  • Excited to build and deliver a new model for achieving lasting weight health
  • Creative and flexible, but always puts the patient first
  • Excellent at forging successful and respectful relationships with the entire team

OUR VALUES

Members First. Always.

Every decision starts with one question - Will this improve the health and the experience of the people we serve?

Outcomes That Matter.

We measure success through sustained weight loss and meaningful improvements in cardiometabolic health.

Integrated Care Wins.

Obesity care requires more than medication alone. We combine clinical care, behavior change, and technology into one coordinated care model.

Relentless Improvement.

We continuously learn from outcomes, data, and our experience to refine our care model and raise the standard of obesity treatment.

Great Partners.

We strive to be easy to work with and trusted by patients, employers, clinicians, partners, and our fellow Calibraters.

Calibrate is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace, providing equal employment and advancement opportunities to all team members. To achieve our mission of changing the way the world treats weight, we are building an environment where every Calibrater can thrive, feel a sense of belonging, and do the best work of their careers. We value diversity and recruit, hire, and promote individuals solely based on talent, qualifications, competence, and merit. Microservices Security Specialist

Location: Centurion, Gauteng (provisional – to be confirmed)
Positions Available: 5
Salary: Market-related
Employment Type: To be confirmed

Job Overview

We are seeking experienced and technically proficient Microservices Security Specialists to design, implement, manage and continuously improve security controls across enterprise microservices architectures, containerised applications and cloud-native environments.

The successful candidates will be responsible for securing distributed applications, APIs, containers, Kubernetes environments and service-to-service communications against cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities and unauthorised access.

This role requires strong hands-on expertise in microservices security, API protection, container security, DevSecOps, secure application architecture and cloud-native security technologies.

The ideal candidates will have proven experience implementing security controls within enterprise microservices environments, with a strong understanding of secure software development, application security testing, identity management and Zero Trust security principles.

Key Responsibilities

Microservices Security Architecture and Implementation

  • Design, implement and maintain security controls across enterprise microservices architectures.
  • Conduct security assessments of distributed applications and microservices environments.
  • Identify and remediate security vulnerabilities within microservices, APIs and supporting infrastructure.
  • Implement secure communication mechanisms between microservices and distributed applications.
  • Apply Zero Trust principles to service-to-service authentication and authorisation.
  • Support the development of secure microservices architecture standards and security design patterns.
  • Conduct threat modelling and security architecture reviews for cloud-native applications.
  • Collaborate with software architects and development teams to implement security-by-design principles.
  • Ensure microservices security controls align with organisational security policies and recognised industry standards.

API Security and Service-to-Service Protection

  • Implement and maintain security controls for RESTful APIs, GraphQL APIs and microservices endpoints.
  • Configure secure API authentication and authorisation mechanisms.
  • Implement OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JSON Web Tokens (JWT) and mutual TLS (mTLS).
  • Secure API gateways and manage API access policies.
  • Identify and mitigate common API vulnerabilities, including those outlined in the OWASP API Security Top 10.
  • Implement API rate limiting, request validation and traffic protection mechanisms.
  • Secure service-to-service communications within distributed environments.
  • Monitor API security events and investigate suspicious access patterns.
  • Support API security testing and vulnerability remediation.

Container and Kubernetes Security

  • Implement security controls across Docker and Kubernetes environments.
  • Conduct container image vulnerability assessments and security configuration reviews.
  • Secure container registries, runtime environments and orchestration platforms.
  • Configure Kubernetes Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), network policies and workload security controls.
  • Implement secure secrets management and container authentication mechanisms.
  • Monitor container and Kubernetes security events.
  • Identify and remediate misconfigurations within containerised environments.
  • Apply security hardening standards to Kubernetes clusters and workloads.
  • Support container runtime protection and cloud-native threat detection.
  • Collaborate with infrastructure and DevOps teams to maintain secure container platforms.

DevSecOps and Secure Software Development

  • Integrate security controls into software development and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Implement automated application security testing within development workflows.
  • Support Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) and Software Composition Analysis (SCA).
  • Identify vulnerabilities in application code, third-party dependencies and container images.
  • Implement secure coding standards and software supply chain security controls.
  • Support Infrastructure as Code (IaC) security scanning and configuration validation.
  • Collaborate with development teams to remediate security findings.
  • Promote secure software development lifecycle (SSDLC) practices.
  • Support continuous security monitoring and automated compliance checks.

Cloud-Native Security and Infrastructure Protection

  • Implement security controls for microservices deployed across Microsoft Azure, AWS or Google Cloud environments.
  • Secure cloud-native application platforms and managed Kubernetes services.
  • Configure network segmentation and secure connectivity between microservices.
  • Implement cloud identity and access management controls.
  • Secure application secrets, cryptographic keys and sensitive configuration information.
  • Support service mesh security implementations.
  • Implement workload identity and secure service authentication.
  • Assess cloud-native infrastructure for vulnerabilities and security misconfigurations.
  • Support security monitoring, logging and incident response within distributed application environments.

Security Monitoring, Risk Management and Compliance

  • Monitor microservices and API security events using relevant security monitoring tools.
  • Investigate application security incidents and coordinate remediation activities.
  • Conduct vulnerability assessments and security risk reviews.
  • Maintain security documentation, assessment reports and remediation records.
  • Support security audits and compliance assessments involving cloud-native applications.
  • Implement security controls aligned with ISO 27001, NIST and OWASP guidance.
  • Monitor emerging microservices, container and API security threats.
  • Recommend improvements to application security architecture and operational processes.
  • Provide technical guidance to development, DevOps and infrastructure teams.

Minimum Requirements

  • Relevant diploma or degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Cybersecurity, Information Security or a related discipline.
  • Typically 3–5 years of relevant experience in application security, DevSecOps, cloud-native security or microservices security.
  • Proven hands-on experience implementing security controls within microservices or distributed application environments.
  • Strong understanding of microservices architecture and secure application design principles.
  • Practical experience securing REST APIs and service-to-service communications.
  • Strong knowledge of OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT and TLS/mTLS.
  • Experience implementing or assessing security controls within Docker and Kubernetes environments.
  • Understanding of Kubernetes RBAC, network policies, secrets management and container security.
  • Experience with application security testing tools and methodologies.
  • Knowledge of OWASP Top 10 and OWASP API Security Top 10.
  • Experience integrating security controls into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Familiarity with cloud-native platforms such as Microsoft Azure, AWS or Google Cloud.
  • Understanding of secure software development lifecycle and DevSecOps principles.
  • Experience conducting vulnerability assessments and coordinating security remediation.
  • Strong technical troubleshooting, analytical and documentation skills.

Technical Skills and Competencies

Microservices and Application Security

  • Microservices architecture and distributed systems
  • Secure application architecture
  • Microservices threat modelling
  • Service-to-service authentication and authorisation
  • Zero Trust application security
  • Secure software development lifecycle
  • Application vulnerability assessments
  • Secure coding principles
  • OWASP Top 10
  • OWASP API Security Top 10

API Security Technologies

  • GraphQL API security
  • OAuth 2.0
  • OpenID Connect (OIDC)
  • JSON Web Tokens (JWT)
  • Mutual TLS (mTLS)
  • API authentication and authorisation
  • API gateways
  • API rate limiting and request validation
  • API vulnerability testing

Experience with platforms such as:

  • Azure API Management
  • AWS API Gateway
  • Kong Gateway
  • Apigee
  • NGINX
  • Other enterprise API management and security solutions

Container and Kubernetes Security

  • Container runtime security

  • Kubernetes security hardening

  • Other container and Kubernetes security platforms

DevSecOps and Application Security Testing

  • Software supply chain security

  • Envoy
  • Service mesh security
  • Mutual TLS
  • Service identity

  • Service-to-service authorisation
  • Secure ingress and egress controls
  • Network segmentation

Automation and Infrastructure as Code

Security Monitoring and Incident Response

  • Cloud-native threat detection

  • Vulnerability management
  • Security incident investigation
  • Threat detection and remediation

Security Frameworks and Standards

  • OWASP Top 10
  • OWASP API Security Top 10
  • OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS)
  • NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF)

  • ISO/IEC 27001

Relevant Certifications (Advantageous)

One or more of the following certifications would be beneficial:

  • Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist (CKS)
  • Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA)
  • Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD)
  • Certified Cloud Security Professional (CCSP)
  • Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
  • Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH)
  • CompTIA Security+
  • Microsoft Certified: Azure Security Engineer Associate

  • Relevant DevSecOps, application security or cloud-native security certifications

Key Personal Attributes

  • Strong analytical and technical problem-solving abilities.
  • Excellent understanding of modern application security threats.

  • Ability to identify and remediate complex microservices security vulnerabilities.
  • Proactive approach to secure application development and infrastructure protection.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with development, DevOps, cloud and cybersecurity teams.
  • Strong organisational and technical documentation skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple security priorities and technical projects.
  • High levels of confidentiality, accountability and professional integrity.

Application Requirements

Interested candidates should submit an updated CV clearly detailing their practical microservices security, API security, container security and DevSecOps experience, together with copies of relevant academic qualifications and professional certifications.

Candidates should specifically highlight:

  • Microservices architectures and distributed application environments they have secured.

  • Practical experience with Docker, Kubernetes and container security.
  • OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT and mutual TLS implementation experience.

  • Service mesh security, workload identity and secrets management experience.
  • Security tools, platforms and technologies they have implemented or administered.
  • Relevant microservices security, application security and cloud-native security projects.
  • Professional certifications and specialised technical training.

Important: This is a specialist Microservices Security opportunity requiring demonstrable hands-on experience securing microservices architectures, APIs and cloud-native applications. General software development, infrastructure administration or cybersecurity experience without substantial microservices security expertise will not be sufficient.

This role is open to candidates based in Johor Bahru, Kuala Lumpur, or Penang, Malaysia. The position is remote with regional travel as required.

Client Overview

Our client is a publicly traded healthcare technology company specializing in digital musculoskeletal (MSK) healthcare solutions. The company combines advanced wearable sensors, computer vision technology, and clinical care to deliver accessible and technology-driven healthcare solutions at scale.

With a strong presence across the healthcare technology ecosystem, the organization works with enterprise clients, health plans, healthcare providers, and strategic partners to improve patient outcomes while reducing healthcare costs. Its technology portfolio includes connected hardware and digital health solutions that require robust manufacturing, quality, and supply chain processes.

As the company continues to scale its hardware and medical device operations, it is seeking an experienced Manufacturing & Quality Engineer to strengthen manufacturing processes, supplier quality, product validation, and production readiness across its hardware ecosystem.

Job Role

The Senior Manufacturing & Quality Engineer – Medical Devices & Consumer Electronics will play a key role in ensuring that hardware products, manufacturing processes, fixtures, tooling, and quality systems are designed, validated, and maintained for efficient and reliable mass production.

The role will work closely with contract manufacturers, component suppliers, engineering teams, and internal product and operations stakeholders throughout the product lifecycle—from new product introduction (NPI) through mass production.

The ideal candidate brings strong hands-on experience in manufacturing engineering, quality engineering, mechanical/electrical engineering, or related disciplines, with a proven track record supporting high-volume consumer electronics and/or medical device manufacturing.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the development, validation, implementation, and maintenance of manufacturing processes, fixtures, tooling, and production systems for high-volume manufacturing.
  • Develop and optimize fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging processes to achieve high quality, reliability, efficiency, and cost effectiveness.
  • Ensure component suppliers and contract manufacturers consistently meet product design, fabrication, assembly, testing, and quality requirements.
  • Lead day-to-day execution of hardware quality processes across manufacturing and supplier operations.
  • Support and drive New Product Introduction (NPI) programs from early development through EVT, DVT, PVT, and mass production.
  • Lead yield improvement, cost reduction, process validation, root-cause analysis, and manufacturing efficiency initiatives.
  • Apply pFMEA, Process Validation, CAPA, and structured problem-solving methodologies to identify and resolve manufacturing and quality issues.
  • Collaborate with contract manufacturers under CM, JDM, ODM, and OEM models and ensure clear alignment of responsibilities and quality expectations.
  • Work closely with component suppliers and EMS partners to resolve technical, quality, and production issues.
  • Support the development of a world-class hardware operations and product organization with strong end-to-end manufacturing and supply chain capabilities.
  • Engage with contract manufacturers and suppliers remotely and onsite as required.
  • Communicate complex technical issues clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Drive consensus and effective collaboration across engineering, product, operations, quality, and supplier teams.
  • Travel within the region as required to support suppliers, manufacturing sites, and project activities.

Candidate Requirements

  • Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Quality Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • Minimum 9+ years of professional experience, preferably with 10+ years in manufacturing process support, manufacturing engineering, or quality engineering roles.
  • Proven experience taking hardware products from product development through NPI and mass production in high-volume manufacturing environments.
  • Strong experience in consumer electronics and/or electro-mechanical medical device manufacturing.
  • Hands-on knowledge of manufacturing and qualification processes including injection molding, metal fabrication, electronic components, SMT, batteries, FATP, and packaging.
  • Extensive experience working with EMS contract manufacturers under CM, JDM, ODM, and/or OEM models.
  • Strong understanding of EVT, DVT, PVT, and Mass Production phase-gate methodologies, including pFMEA and process validation.
  • Practical experience with QMS, CAPA, supplier quality management, and quality compliance for medical devices, preferably Class II or Class III products.
  • Knowledge of relevant medical device standards and regulatory requirements, including FDA and ISO 13485.
  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional projects involving yield improvement, cost reduction, process validation, and manufacturing efficiency.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, including practical use of structured quality tools such as the 7 QC tools.
  • Working knowledge of embedded systems and functional testing is an advantage.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across Manufacturing, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Product, and Contract Manufacturing teams.
  • Strong ability to simplify complex technical issues and communicate them effectively to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Self-driven, proactive, adaptable, and comfortable working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
  • Willingness and ability to travel regionally as required.
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and Slack is preferred.
  • Knowledge or experience in AI and CAD is an added advantage.
  • Fluency in English, Mandarin Chinese, and Malay is required, both written and verbal.

jobs.title: Release Manager
jobs.excerpt: The Release Manager owns the mechanics of moving code from merge to production across every Delivery Team.
jobs.description:
The Release Manager owns the mechanics of moving code from merge to production across every Delivery Team. You are air traffic control for each release: you know what is in it and what is not, you coordinate the teams contributing to it, you own the technical and business go/no-go, and you drive it from cut to landed. You also own the environments, pipeline, and change-control record that make releases safe and auditable.

This is not a runbook-execution seat. You are expected to understand why the release process works, handle non-standard releases on their merits, and continuously improve the process.

Job Responsibilities & Major Functions

  • Release Execution: Execute Standard and Limited (audience-scoped) releases, including configuring and verifying audience scoping. Execute approved hotfixes: cut the branch, ship it, close it out. Define the rollback path per release type, make the call when a deployment fails technically, and run it.
  • Release Readiness: Own the technical and business go/no-go on every grouped release, including Release Readiness and Milestone Reviews: are the changes shippable, are dependencies present, has the migration path been rehearsed, and is the business ready for it. Surface technical coupling and deployment-ordering constraints when release contents are decided, and handle non-standard releases such as running a migration separately, staging a two-phase deploy, or sequencing a schema change ahead of dependent code. Produce a release manifest for every release (contents, teams, commits, migrations, and configuration changes).
  • Branch and Repository Hygiene: Enforce the branching model across every repository: branch creation, merge and squash discipline, cherry-picks into release branches, release branch cut and close, and tag and version discipline. Gate what enters a release branch after cut, and keep release branches free of drift, orphans, and long-lived unmerged work.
  • Environment Ownership: Own the known-state, availability, and scheduling of Devtest, Acceptance, Beta, and Production, including data refresh and configuration parity so QA validates against something representative.
  • Deployment Pipeline: Own the build-promotion and deployment pipeline end to end, drive out manual steps, and verify that each deployment landed cleanly.
  • Process and Reporting: Keep deploy-pending and validation statuses accurate so "what is going out next" is answerable from the board. Report release frequency against plan, cycle time from code-complete to production, failed-deployment rate, rollback rate, hotfix rate, and hotfix-to-scheduled-release ratio. Run a short retrospective on any failed or rolled-back release, and own release runbooks and documentation.
  • Change Control and Audit Evidence: Produce and retain the change-control record for every production push: what changed, who approved it, what validation passed, when it went out, and the rollback path. Serve as the system of record for release history in security, compliance, and customer audits.
  • Release Communication: Derive cut dates and code-freeze windows from the Technical Delivery Manager’s release calendar, communicate them, and enforce them at the branch. Communicate release details and schedules to the business, including Sales, CS, and leadership. Notify teams and stakeholders of deployment start, completion, and failure in real time, and coordinate cross-team release dependencies before cut.

Scope Boundaries

This role operates within clear lines so ownership never overlaps:

  • The Technical Delivery Manager owns SDLC process, cadence, the release calendar, and hotfix decisions.
  • The Enterprise Application Architect defines branching strategy and code-quality standards; this role operates and enforces them.
  • Infrastructure engineering owns provisioning, cloud infrastructure, IaC, CI runners, and platform tooling; this role owns environments and the pipeline as release resources.
  • Tech Leads drive fixes to done; Project Managers own sprint blockers and business-impact escalation; Product Marketing owns customer-facing communication.

About You

You are process-first, and you write things down. You automate a repeated manual step rather than executing it well twice. You can tell a team it missed the cut, with no authority over the people you are gating, and hold that line under pressure. When your own release fails, you run a blameless post-mortem on it.

Requirements

Requirements (Must-Haves)

  • U.S. citizenship and full-time U.S. residency, driven by contractual obligations with our customers.
  • Availability for off-hours release work. Releases commonly run outside business hours, and this role must be reliably present for most of them on a sustainable schedule.

Qualifications

  • Strong Git competency, the top technical priority: branching strategies, merges and squashes, cherry-picking, tagging, and managing the Git workflows that underpin a release process.
  • Strong technical fluency. Not a software engineer or DBA, but a working mental model of CI/CD pipelines, containers and images, build artifacts, frontend vs. backend systems, deployment architecture, and MySQL concepts such as migrations, indexes, and the impact of database changes.
  • Proven release management experience in a SaaS environment, including managing multiple releases concurrently across cross-functional teams.
  • Excellent project and process management: tracking scope, chasing dependencies, enforcing process at the gate, and designing process where none exists.
  • Strong communication and documentation skills, working closely with Engineering, QA, Product, and CS.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Strongly Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior software engineering, engineering management, Agile/Scrum/Ops, or database experience.
  • AWS familiarity.
  • Regulated-industry release experience (HIPAA, SOC 2, FedRAMP change control).
  • Zero-downtime deployment and database migration experience.
  • Feature-flag or progressive-delivery experience, directly relevant to Limited Releases.
  • Scripting and automation experience, plus familiarity with defect tracking and configuration management tools.
