jobs.description:
CloudLinux builds Linux infrastructure and security products. You will join our Automation & Management Services cell, working closely with Dmitrii Petrov to solve problems across teams and services: cloud-cost data, infrastructure inventory, network policies and capacity workflows.

Check out our website for more information

Inside the Infrastructure Department, the Platform cell is a small team. We run the observability platform, the company's GitLab and the CI runners behind it, a few smaller engineering services, and the automation the department relies on for provisioning and configuration.

We are looking for a Platform Engineer for the PaaS team to take ownership of an agreed set of platform services: keep them reliable and within agreed service levels, make changes and recovery repeatable, and reduce recurring operational work through automation and self-service.

You get real freedom in how you implement things, and you own the result: you pick the approach, defend it in review, and answer for how the service behaves afterwards.

Most of the job is what site reliability engineering is about: services that run well day after day, and requests from product teams handled properly. Some of it is building. The observability platform and the runner cluster were both built from scratch within the last year, and there will be more of that. Expect the work to split between platform engineering, incident response, and helping engineers in other teams use what we run.

What you'll do

  • Run the observability platform. Keep it healthy, onboard teams, watch cost and capacity, and maintain the alerting that runs on top of it.
  • Run GitLab and the CI runner fleet. Upgrades, capacity, access, backups and restore drills.
  • Keep the rest of our services healthy, with the monitoring and runbooks a production service needs.
  • Deploy new services when they are requested. Research the options, pick a design, and stand the service up from scratch according to good practice: as code, monitored, backed up, documented.
  • Work with developers' requests. Access, onboarding, pipeline problems, new exporters and dashboards. Answer them, and turn the recurring ones into self-service.
  • Run incidents. Diagnose and mitigate impact, restore service safely, then complete the root-cause analysis and post-mortem. Deliver the prevention or detection improvements the incident calls for.
  • Ship everything as code, reviewed in merge requests. Plan and check before every change.
  • Write for engineers outside the team. Runbooks, onboarding guides, maintenance notices and status updates that people can act on.
  • Work with AI agents. Delegate collection and drafting to them, review their output as you would a colleague's merge request, and record what you learn where the team can find it.

Requirements

Must have:

  • Senior-level experience in infrastructure, platform or site reliability engineering, including at least one production service you were responsible for keeping up. We will ask you to walk us through it in detail: what broke, how you found out, and what you changed so it would not happen again.
  • Linux systems administration and debugging on bare metal and virtual machines. Much of our infrastructure is not Kubernetes.
  • Kubernetes in production delivered through GitOps, including cluster upgrades you performed yourself.
  • Infrastructure as code as your delivery form: Ansible and Terraform or OpenTofu, changes reviewed in merge requests.
  • GitLab administration and GitLab CI in production, self-hosted or SaaS. Deep experience with another CI system is acceptable if you can show the same depth.
  • Working knowledge of the Prometheus and Grafana ecosystem: you have run it for a team, written alert rules and dashboards, and can read PromQL. Depth here is welcome, and learnable.
  • Written technical explanation for engineers outside your team: runbooks, notices, answers to requests.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills. This role deals with people at least as much as with servers: most work starts as a conversation with a product team, and you need to understand what they actually need, agree scope, priority and timing with them, push back politely when a request should not be done as asked, and keep everyone informed while the work is in progress. We are looking for someone other teams enjoy working with.
  • Advanced use of AI engineering assistants such as Claude and Codex: providing context, breaking down tasks, designing agent loops, and delegating plans for unattended, end-to-end execution within defined scope and permissions, with clear stop conditions. You can explain, debug and test the resulting automation, and verify generated commands, scripts and conclusions before they touch production.
  • English - upper-intermediate or higher - to ensure clear communication of progress within the teams.

Nice to have:

  • Alerting design: SLOs, burn-rate alerts, thresholds sized from data.
  • MicroVM isolation for CI: Kata Containers, Firecracker or gVisor.
  • S3-compatible object storage operations: Ceph RGW or similar.
  • AWS with real cost work.
  • Self-hosted Sentry, or another Kafka, ClickHouse and Redis-backed application you have kept alive under load.
  • Python or Go for exporters and small internal services.

You do not need to have run every system on this list. Solid fundamentals and the judgment to pick up an unfamiliar service, make it observable and hand back a runbook matter more than matching every line.

What this role is not focused on:

  • Not a ticket-queue operator. Recurring requests get turned into self-service, not processed one by one forever.
  • Not a pure cloud or Kubernetes role. Bare metal and virtual machines are a large part of our infrastructure.
  • Not the DBA, the network engineer or the security engineer. Those teams run their own systems; we provide the platform they monitor them with.

Benefits

What's in it for you?

  • A focus on professional development.

jobs.title: Information Assistant
jobs.excerpt: Samba is a media intelligence company.  We know what the world is watching, reading, and thinking about — in real time, at scale, across every screen.
jobs.description:
Samba is a media intelligence company. We know what the world is watching, reading, and thinking about — in real time, at scale, across every screen. Our data exists with the consent of over a billion people, organized into the most complete picture of consumer attention ever built. The biggest brands in the world use that picture to make smarter decisions. We think it’s the most interesting data asset on the planet, because it’s the most culturally relevant.

Nine countries. Fifteen people on the team. Not nearly enough of them free on Sundays. That's the gap you'd fill.

Our system records linear TV channels and pulls out everything that might be an ad. Only a fraction of it actually is. The team, mostly contractors across Poland and Italy plus a few colleagues in the US, decides which clips are ads and which aren't, then tags the ones that are. We're adding another market in January, volume keeps growing, and right now the team is stretched thin. Sundays most of all.

What you'd actually do

Look at what the system flags, decide whether it's an ad, and apply the metadata, following the rulebook for that country. There are a lot of rules, and every market has its own. You'd start with a structured training block with Riccardo, then work the queue alongside the team. German is the language we're thinnest on, so that's the one we're hiring for first.

It's repetitive, especially in the first weeks.

What you need to already be good at

    • Fluent English and German. You'll work in both

    • Steady, structured work. Office, shifts, client-facing, whatever it was, you know what showing up consistently looks like

    • Attention to detail. You can follow a long rulebook and apply it the same way on the hundredth clip as on the first

    • 32–40 hours a week, every Sunday

      • Bonus points

      French · Italian · Polish · Spanish · subtitling, transcription or localization QC · content moderation or data labelling · familiarity with TV advertising and brands

      Not for you if

      • "Information specialist" sounds like databases and queries to you. It's not that job. Nobody here will ask you to write SQL.

      • You need variety to stay engaged. You'll be making the same kind of decision all day.

      • Sundays are negotiable. They aren't, and we won't rotate them.

      • You're looking for a stopgap to leave in a few months. Training takes real time, and we're hiring someone to stay.

        • How we judge you, and how it goes

        Skills we teach, attitude we don't. Every hire is scored on the same five things: determined yet resilient, naturally curious, low-ego, self-aware, results oriented. For this role that means: you keep your quality up when the work is repetitive, you ask when a rule doesn't fit, you're good with a team that's stretched, you know honestly whether this work suits you, and your tagging is right.

        Riccardo is watching for one thing above all: that you understand what the job is from the start, and that you're reliable.

        Why now

        We're Series C, ~$100M raised, pre-IPO, growing 30% YoY, 18 years in. For this team, that growth means more markets and more volume. Another country comes online in January, and we want you trained before it does.

Job Description: PCI Internal Security Assessor (ISA)

Department: Enterprise Security & Technology Risk Management Location: Regionwide

Reports To: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)

Job Overview

The PCI Internal Security Assessor (ISA) is responsible for ensuring that our client from banking industry complies with the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS). The ISA will assess, monitor, and enforce the security measures necessary to protect cardholder data and maintain PCI compliance across all systems and processes. This role works closely with internal stakeholders and external parties to maintain a secure environment, mitigate risks, and improve overall security posture.

Key Responsibilities:

  • PCI DSS Compliance Management:
    • Conduct regular internal assessments and audits to ensure the organization's compliance with PCI DSS.

Develop and implement PCI compliance policies, procedures, and controls.

  • Serve as the internal point of contact for PCI DSS-related matters and ensure all applicable security controls are in place.
  • Collaborate with the external Qualified Security Assessor (QSA) to facilitate annual PCI DSS certification audits.

Documentation and Reporting:

  • Prepare and maintain comprehensive documentation, including policies, procedures, and reports required for PCI DSS compliance.
  • Maintain comprehensive documentation of assessment findings, corrective actions, and compliance status.
  • Manage the submission of the Self-Assessment Questionnaires (SAQs) and Attestation of Compliance documents (AOCs) as needed.

Qualifications:

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Computer Science, or a related field (or

equivalent work experience).

  • Experience:
    • Minimum of 3-5 years of experience in information security, PCI compliance, or a related field.
    • Previous experience as an ISA, QSA, or a similar role is highly desirable.
  • Certifications:
    • Certified PCI Internal Security Assessor (ISA) or Certified PCI Professional (PCIP) certifications preferred.

Additional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, or CEH are a plus.

  • Skills and Competencies:
    • Deep understanding of PCI DSS requirements and data security best practices.
    • Familiarity with security frameworks (NIST, ISO 27001, CIS Controls) and security technologies (firewalls, IDS/IPS, encryption, etc.).
    • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills.
    • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to work cross- functionally.
    • Proficiency in using security assessment tools and techniques (e.g., vulnerability scanners, SIEM).

Other Requirements:

Ability to work independently and handle sensitive information confidentially.

  • Detail-oriented with strong organizational skills.
  • Occasional travel may be required for audits or compliance reviews.
  • Risk Assessment and Mitigation:
    • Identify and assess potential risks to cardholder data environments and provide recommendations for risk mitigation.
    • Implement and enforce necessary security controls to address gaps identified during assessments.
    • Ensure vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, and security reviews are conducted to identify weaknesses and ensure continuous compliance.
  • Training and Awareness:
    • Conduct internal PCI DSS training for staff to ensure a deep understanding of the importance of compliance and security measures.
    • Provide ongoing guidance and support to departments regarding security best practices related to PCI DSS.
  • Collaboration and Communication:
    • Work closely with projects, Enterprise Security, Technology, and other relevant departments to align PCI DSS compliance with overall security policies and practices.
    • Proactively identify and/or promptly escalate risks and issues affecting PCI compliance status.
    • Stay updated on changes in PCI DSS requirements and industry best practices to ensure our client from banking industry remains compliant.
    • Present PCI DSS compliance status reports to senior management and external stakeholders.

jobs.excerpt: Job Description SummaryAs a Staff Research Scientist – Reconstruction Physics, you will provide scientific leadership for next-generation reconstruction technologies in quantitative nuclear medicine imaging.
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

As a Staff Research Scientist – Reconstruction Physics, you will provide scientific leadership for next-generation reconstruction technologies in quantitative nuclear medicine imaging. You will lead research initiatives focused on SPECT image reconstruction, physics modeling, uncertainty quantification, and quantitative imaging methods, while helping shape both the GE HealthCare software product roadmap and the broader scientific direction of the field.

This role is intended for an internationally recognized expert who combines deep technical expertise with demonstrated influence across the research community. In addition to driving high-impact research programs, you will represent GE HealthCare through publications, scientific working groups, conference participation, and external collaborations that advance quantitative imaging science.

You will work closely with research, engineering, clinical science, product management, and external academic partners to translate emerging scientific advances into clinically meaningful innovations.

GE Healthcare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities:


Scientific Leadership

  • Define and lead strategic research programs in medical image reconstruction, quantitative imaging, and imaging physics.
  • Establish scientific direction for reconstruction technologies that support future GE HealthCare product innovation, including our MIM Software product suite.
  • Identify emerging scientific opportunities and guide long-term research investments in reconstruction and quantitative imaging.
  • Lead cross-functional project teams, coordinating scientists, engineers, clinical experts, and external collaborators to deliver high-impact research outcomes.

Research and Technical Innovation

  • Design, prototype, and evaluate novel reconstruction algorithms and physics-based imaging methods.
  • Apply advanced modeling, inverse problem techniques, numerical optimization, and statistical methods to challenging imaging problems.
  • Drive innovation beyond established approaches and contribute new scientific advances to the field.
  • Develop high-quality software prototypes that demonstrate and validate new concepts.

External Scientific Leadership

  • Maintain global expertise and scientific domain intellectual leadership both inside and outside GEHC.
  • Represent GE HealthCare in scientific working groups, standards efforts, and professional organizations.
  • Publish research findings in peer-reviewed journals and present results at leading scientific conferences.
  • Build and maintain collaborations with academic institutions, research consortia, government agencies, and industry partners.
  • Help shape the future direction of quantitative imaging and reconstruction science through visible technical leadership and community engagement.

Cross-Functional Influence

  • Partner with clinical, engineering, product, and business leaders to align research strategy with customer and market needs.
  • Influence technical roadmaps across multiple programs and organizational boundaries.
  • Serve as a trusted scientific advisor to internal stakeholders and leadership teams.

Mentorship and Capability Building

  • Mentor scientists and engineers across the organization.
  • Promote scientific rigor, reproducibility, and technical excellence.
  • Strengthen organizational capability through knowledge sharing, technical reviews, and research leadership.

Required Qualifications

  • Advanced degree (PhD strongly preferred) in Biomedical Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or a related discipline.
  • Deep expertise in medical imaging algorithms with significant experience in image reconstruction.
  • Demonstrated record of scientific innovation and independent research leadership.
  • Strong foundation in numerical methods, inverse problems, optimization, and statistical modeling.
  • Experience leading complex technical initiatives involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

Desired Characteristics

  • Recognized expertise in SPECT or other tomographic imaging modalities.
  • Expertise in Monte Carlo simulation and physics-based system modeling.
  • Experience in quantitative nuclear medicine imaging and theranostics.
  • Record of influential publications, invited presentations, patents, or other widely recognized scientific contributions.
  • Experience leading external collaborations, multi-institution research programs, or scientific working groups.
  • Experience mentoring researchers and providing technical leadership across organizations.
  • Familiarity with machine learning and AI methods relevant to medical imaging.

You'll Thrive Here If You

  • Are motivated to advance the state of the art, not just deliver incremental product improvements.
  • Enjoy connecting academic innovation with meaningful clinical impact.
  • Want to help define future scientific directions for quantitative imaging and reconstruction.
  • Can influence technical strategy both inside and outside the organization.
  • Value collaboration and enjoy building communities around important scientific challenges.

We expect all employees to live and breathe our behaviors: to act with humility and build trust; lead with transparency; deliver with focus, and drive ownership –always with unyielding integrity.

Our total rewards are designed to unlock your ambition by giving you the boost and flexibility you need to turn your ideas into world-changing realities. Our salary and benefits are everything you’d expect from an organization with global strength and scale, and you’ll be surrounded by career opportunities in a culture that fosters care, collaboration and support.

  • Realizar e apoiar Análises de Impacto à Proteção de Dados (DPIA/RIPD);
  • Apoiar a elaboração, revisão e atualização de políticas, normas, procedimentos e diretrizes de privacidade;
  • Orientar áreas como TI, RH, Marketing e demais áreas de negócio sobre boas práticas de proteção de dados;
  • Apoiar a elaboração e revisão de termos, avisos de privacidade e documentos relacionados ao tratamento de dados pessoais;
  • Atuar no atendimento e acompanhamento de solicitações de titulares de dados;
  • Apoiar o relacionamento com áreas internas e, quando aplicável, com autoridades reguladoras;
  • Identificar oportunidades de melhoria nos processos relacionados à privacidade e proteção de dados;
  • Apoiar ações de conscientização e treinamentos sobre privacidade e proteção de dados.

O que precisamos que você tenha de conhecimento:

  • Ensino superior completo em Direito, Ciência da Computação, Segurança da Informação, Administração ou áreas correlatas;
  • Experiência com Proteção de Dados, Privacidade ou Compliance;
  • Conhecimento da LGPD e seus principais conceitos e requisitos;
  • Conhecimento de boas práticas e conceitos relacionados ao GDPR será considerado;
  • Experiência com mapeamento de processos e dados pessoais;
  • Conhecimentos em gestão de riscos relacionados à privacidade;
  • Noções de Segurança da Informação e Cibersegurança;
  • Conhecimento em elaboração e revisão de políticas, procedimentos e documentos de privacidade;
  • Boa comunicação e facilidade para interação com diferentes áreas da organização.

Diferenciais:

  • Experiência com DPIA/RIPD;
  • Certificações ou cursos em Privacidade e Proteção de Dados;
  • Experiência com ferramentas de GRC, Privacy Management ou Data Mapping;

jobs.excerpt: Become a part of our caring community Technology is one of the organization’s largest, fastest-changing and most strategically important areas of external investment.
jobs.description:
Become a part of our caring community

Technology is one of the organization’s largest, fastest-changing and most strategically important areas of external investment. The Associate Vice President, IT Procurement & Supplier Management will lead a 40+ associate organization responsible for converting annual technology spend into business capability, innovation, speed, resilience and financial value.

The AVP will serve as the senior Procurement partner to the Technology Leadership Team and reshape how Technology, Procurement and the supplier ecosystem work together.

The role leads category and supplier management across enterprise software and SaaS, cloud and infrastructure, hardware, telecommunications, technology labor, consulting, managed services and other technology-enabled services. Working across Technology, Finance, Legal, Risk, Privacy, Information Security and Procurement, the AVP will engage earlier in strategy and investment planning, improve supplier economics and performance, strengthen commercial leverage, reduce friction and cycle time, and build a commercially sophisticated, analytically rigorous and technology-enabled team.

Success will be measured by whether Technology moves faster, makes better investment decisions and receives greater value, innovation and resilience from its supplier ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as Technology’s Strategic Commercial Partner

  • Serve as the senior Procurement relationship leader and trusted commercial advisor to the Technology Leadership Team.
  • Translate Technology strategy, architecture, investment priorities and multi-year roadmaps into integrated category, supplier and commercial strategies.
  • Connect Technology planning and funding decisions with Procurement’s sourcing pipeline, renewal calendar and value commitments.
  • Engage before requirements and supplier preferences are fixed, helping leaders evaluate make, buy, partner, renew, consolidate and exit alternatives.
  • Shape demand, challenge unnecessary complexity and clarify the total cost, risk and strategic implications of commercial decisions.
  • Bring external market intelligence, supplier perspectives and competitive alternatives into Technology planning.
  • Deliver concise, decision-ready executive recommendations covering value, cost, risk, contractual exposure, optionality and tradeoffs.
  • Establish Procurement as an extension of Technology leadership rather than a downstream execution function.

Accelerate Execution and Simplify the Experience

  • Lead the overall Technology-Procurement commercial experience while maintaining clear decision rights across enterprise functions.
  • Identify and remove bottlenecks across intake, sourcing, due diligence, contracting, approvals and renewals.
  • Establish transparent service levels, ownership, escalation paths and performance measures.
  • Create differentiated pathways based on value, complexity and risk so routine work moves quickly and consequential decisions receive appropriate rigor.
  • Use intake, orchestration, analytics and automation to improve transparency, data quality and cross-functional coordination.
  • Reduce fire drills through disciplined demand and renewal planning, early risk identification and clear executive decision calendars.
  • Build a culture of urgency, accountability and practical problem-solving focused on measurable speed-to-value.

Lead Category Strategy and Enterprise Value Creation

  • Own enterprise strategies for software and SaaS, cloud, infrastructure, hardware, telecommunications, technology labor, consulting and managed services.
  • Develop multi-year category strategies grounded in Technology roadmaps, architecture direction, consumption data, market intelligence, benchmarks, cost drivers and emerging technologies.
  • Maintain a forward-looking portfolio of sourcing, renewal, optimization, demand-management and supplier-transformation opportunities sufficient to meet enterprise-value commitments.
  • Drive value beyond price through license and consumption optimization, demand reduction, supplier and application rationalization, labor productivity, commercial-model redesign, contractual value recovery, working capital, risk reduction and supplier innovation.
  • Partner with Technology Finance to connect commitments, utilization, consumption and forecasts with realized financial outcomes.
  • Evaluate total Technology economics, including implementation, integration, migration, support, adoption, exit costs and technical-debt implications.
  • Personally lead or sponsor the organization’s most complex, highest-value and highest-risk Technology negotiations.
  • Build negotiation strategies using supplier economics, benchmarks, competitive alternatives, contractual rights, switching costs and enterprise-wide leverage.
  • Establish disciplined renewal planning that creates leverage well before deadlines and eliminates surprise renewals.
  • Partner with Finance to establish credible baselines and ensure commercial outcomes translate into measurable enterprise impact.

Shape the Technology Supplier Ecosystem

  • Lead Supplier Managers responsible for strategic and enterprise-critical Technology suppliers.
  • Segment suppliers based on criticality, value, dependency, concentration, switching complexity and risk.
  • Define the strategic role each critical supplier should play in the future Technology ecosystem.
  • Establish executive governance, supplier scorecards, performance expectations, issue-management disciplines and joint value plans.
  • Hold suppliers accountable for service, contractual commitments, commercial competitiveness, productivity, innovation and business outcomes.
  • Coordinate relationships with suppliers serving multiple areas of the enterprise to create one company position and stronger negotiating leverage.
  • Use strategic suppliers to identify emerging capabilities, market shifts and innovation opportunities.
  • Partner across Technology and Risk functions to address cybersecurity, resiliency, concentration, financial, operational, data and fourth-party risks.
  • Establish credible remediation, transition and exit strategies when supplier performance, economics, risk or strategic fit falls short.

Build a High-Performance, Technology-Enabled Team

  • Lead and develop a 40+ associate organization of Category Managers, Supplier Managers and procurement professionals.
  • Set clear expectations for strategic partnership, commercial judgment, speed, accountability, executive communication and enterprise impact.
  • Shift the team from processing demand to shaping decisions, anticipating opportunities and influencing Technology strategy.
  • Build deep capabilities in Technology markets, cloud and consumption economics, software licensing, technology labor, total-cost analysis, category strategy, complex negotiation, supplier economics and executive influence.
  • Increase capacity by simplifying work, standardizing repeatable activities, leveraging shared services and automating work before adding resources.
  • Embed AI, analytics and digital tools into strategy development, negotiation preparation, contract analysis, supplier monitoring and risk identification, with clear human accountability.
  • Hold leaders accountable for outcomes, stakeholder experience, commitments, talent development and organizational health.
  • Strengthen succession readiness and develop leaders who can independently advise senior executives and constructively challenge assumptions.

Modernize the IT Procurement Operating Model

  • Design an integrated operating model connecting Category Management, Supplier Management, sourcing, contracting, Procurement operations, Finance and enterprise centers of excellence.
  • Clarify accountabilities, decision rights and handoffs to eliminate duplication and unnecessary layers.
  • Create an authoritative executive view of Technology demand, active engagements, renewals, supplier performance, contractual exposure, risks and required decisions.
  • Establish a disciplined operating cadence covering category strategy, pipeline, value delivery, cycle time, renewals, supplier performance, risk and talent.
  • Use analytics, market intelligence, contract intelligence and AI to identify opportunities and risks proactively.
  • Improve adoption of preferred suppliers and commercial standards while simplifying the stakeholder experience.
  • Partner with the Chief Procurement Officer and Procurement Leadership Team to advance Procurement as an enterprise force multiplier that improves decisions, accelerates execution and creates greater value.

How Success Will Be Measured

  • Delivery of validated savings, cost avoidance, cost containment, productivity and broader enterprise-value commitments.
  • A finance-aligned opportunity portfolio with sufficient actionable coverage against annual targets.
  • Multi-year category strategies covering the substantial majority of addressable Technology spend.
  • Reliable forward visibility to material demand, renewals, funding decisions and commercial commitments.
  • Elimination of surprise renewals and material reduction in reactive escalations and fire drills.
  • Measurable improvement in sourcing, SOW, contracting and approval cycle times.
  • Clear service levels, ownership and escalation paths across the commercial lifecycle.
  • Strategic suppliers operating under defined relationship strategies, governance, performance measures and joint value plans.
  • Improved supplier performance, commercial competitiveness, innovation, contractual value realization, resilience and risk outcomes.
  • Increased confidence from Technology leadership and greater use of decision-ready Procurement recommendations.
  • More team capacity devoted to strategy, market intelligence, negotiation, executive advisory and supplier value creation.
  • Demonstrated productivity and decision-quality improvements through analytics, automation and AI.
  • Stronger talent retention, succession readiness and internal leadership capability.


Use your skills to make an impact

Required Qualifications

  • 15+ years of progressive experience in Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, Category Management, Supplier Management, Technology Finance or related commercial leadership roles.
  • Significant leadership responsibility for complex Technology spend and supplier portfolios.
  • 7+ years of people leadership experience, including building, transforming and retaining high-performing teams.
  • Deep commercial expertise across several Technology domains, such as software and SaaS, cloud and infrastructure, technology labor, managed services, hardware, telecommunications or consulting.
  • Demonstrated success leading large Technology portfolios and high-value strategic negotiations. Experience with portfolios approaching or exceeding $1 billion in annual spend is strongly preferred.
  • Proven ability to advise CIO-level executives and influence decisions without relying on positional authority.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate Technology and business strategies into category, supplier, demand and commercial strategies.
  • Strong command of licensing, subscription, consumption, capacity, outcome-based and managed-service commercial models.
  • Experience evaluating total cost of ownership, supplier economics, contractual structures, switching costs and value-realization assumptions.
  • Demonstrated success in strategic supplier governance, performance improvement, risk mitigation and executive escalation.
  • Track record of delivering substantial financial value while balancing speed, service, innovation, resilience and enterprise risk.
  • Experience simplifying end-to-end processes, clarifying cross-functional accountability and leading meaningful operating-model change.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a Fortune 500, healthcare, financial services, highly regulated or similarly complex enterprise.
  • Advanced degree or relevant professional certification.
  • Experience with cloud economics, FinOps, software asset management, technology business management or consumption optimization.
  • Experience applying analytics, AI, automation or contract intelligence to improve productivity and decision quality.
  • Experience integrating Category Management and Supplier Management into a unified value model.
  • Experience leading through significant organizational change or enterprise transformation.

jobs.description:
At NI, an Emerson company, we help engineers and organizations solve some of the world's most complex test, measurement, and automation challenges.

As a Senior Partner Development Manager, you will lead the growth of NI's business through select System Integrator partnerships. You will work with executive leaders, sales teams, solution architects, and technical influencers at partner organizations to position NI technology as a preferred component of their solutions and service offerings. This is a highly visible role that combines business development, partner strategy, technical sales, and cross-functional leadership. You will help NI's sales organization to adopt and leverage partners as a preferred route to winning customer opportunities.

Why This Role Matters

System Integrators often influence technology decisions long before a customer makes a purchase. When partners consistently recommend, design with, and deploy NI technology, they create repeatable growth opportunities that scale across industries, applications, and customers.

Success in this role is not only about helping partners adopt NI technology. It is equally about helping NI sales teams understand when and how to engage System Integrator partners to create better customer outcomes. You will serve as the bridge between NI, our partners, and our sales organization, ensuring that the right partners are positioned in the right opportunities and that both organizations work together to drive growth.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and Grow Partner Relationships

  • Build executive, sales, and technical relationships with System Integrator partners across the Americas.

  • Create and execute business plans that align partner growth objectives with NI's strategic priorities.

  • Identify new partnership opportunities and expand existing relationships.

  • Serve as the primary business leader responsible for partner success and growth.

Drive Technology Preference and Solution Adoption

  • Help partners understand where NI technology creates value for their customers.

  • Influence technical decision-makers and solution architects to incorporate NI technology into repeatable customer solutions.

  • Support partners in creating standardized solution offerings that include NI products and platforms.

  • Increase the number of customer projects, proposals, and solutions that leverage NI technology.

Build Scalable Partner Solutions

  • Collaborate with partners to develop packaged service offerings and industry solutions.

  • Work closely with NI product, marketing, and business teams to align partner offerings with market opportunities.

  • Help partners create differentiated value propositions that drive customer adoption.

Enable Partner Sales and Technical Teams

  • Deliver business and technical enablement programs that help partners confidently position NI solutions.

  • Develop tools, training, customer success stories, and solution assets that accelerate partner success.

  • Support partner teams throughout the sales cycle, from opportunity identification through proposal development and customer engagement.

Drive NI Seller Adoption of System Integrator Partners

  • Build awareness, confidence, and preference among NI sales teams for engaging qualified System Integrator partners.

  • Develop strategies that make it easier for NI sellers to identify, access, and leverage partner capabilities in customer opportunities.

  • Create account-mapping initiatives, joint business planning activities, success stories, and sales plays that encourage collaboration between NI sellers and partners.

  • Increase seller-sourced opportunities involving System Integrator partners and improve the effectiveness of partner-led customer engagements.

Ensure Operational Excellence

  • Establish measurable partner growth plans and quarterly business reviews.

  • Track business performance, pipeline development, partner engagement, and strategic initiatives.

  • Maintain strong forecasting discipline and provide visibility into partner-driven business results.

What Success Looks Like

In this role, you will:

  • Consistently achieve or exceed revenue objectives through partner-led and partner-influenced opportunities.

  • Increase the number of customer solutions and service offerings built around NI technology.

  • Grow strategic pipeline and improve win rates in opportunities involving System Integrator partners.

  • Expand executive and technical engagement within partner organizations.

  • Increase the number of NI sales professionals actively leveraging System Integrator partners in customer opportunities.

  • Improve collaboration between NI and partner teams, resulting in measurable business growth and stronger customer outcomes.

  • Establish NI as a preferred technology platform among key System Integrator partners.

Who You Are:

You are a proactive and resourceful professional who acts with urgency and ownership to achieve results. You place customers at the center of your decisions, anticipating needs and delivering exceptional experiences. You build collaborative relationships across functions and establish networks that enable effective partnership and knowledge sharing. You inspire engagement through open communication and a positive team-oriented approach. You are comfortable learning and adopting new technologies and use digital capabilities to improve business outcomes.

For This Role, You Will Need:

  • Bachelor's degree is required, engineering or technical discipline preferred.

  • 10+ years of experience in partner development, business development, strategic alliances, channel sales, account management, or technical sales.

  • Demonstrated success building and growing strategic partner relationships.

  • Experience influencing technical and business stakeholders in complex sales environments.

  • Strong executive presence and the ability to build credibility with senior leaders.

  • Proven ability to lead initiatives across multiple functions and organizations.

  • Strong business planning, forecasting, pipeline management, and operational discipline.

  • Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working for a System Integrator.

  • Experience in test, measurement, industrial automation, manufacturing, software, engineering, or technology markets.

  • Experience developing partner ecosystems and go-to-market strategies.

  • Knowledge of solution-selling and partner-led sales motions.

Our compensation philosophy is simple: we pay a competitive base salary, within the local market in which we operate, and reward performance during our annual merit review process. The salary range for this role is $180,00 - $220,000 annually, plus bonus, commensurate with the skills, talent, capabilities, and experience each candidate brings to a role.

Our Culture & Commitment to You​

​At Emerson, we prioritize a workplace where every employee is valued, respected, and empowered to grow. We foster an environment that encourages innovation, collaboration, and diverse perspectives—because we know that great ideas come from great teams. Our commitment to ongoing career development and growing an inclusive culture ensures you have the support to thrive. Whether through mentorship, training, or leadership opportunities, we invest in your success so you can make a lasting impact. We believe diverse teams, working together are key to driving growth and delivering business results. ​

We recognize the importance of employee wellbeing. We prioritize providing flexible, competitive benefits plans to meet you and your family’s physical, mental, financial, and social needs. We provide a variety of medical insurance plans, with dental and vision coverage, Employee Assistance Program, 401(k), tuition reimbursement, employee resource groups, recognition, and much more. Our culture offers flexible time off plans, including paid parental leave (maternal and paternal), vacation and holiday leave.​

Learn more about our Culture & Values.

This position will be open for a minimum of 7 days from the day of posting. Applicants are encouraged to apply early to receive optimal consideration. Job description

A Snapshot of Curvion Blue:

Curvion Blue is a fast paced, high performance sales agency that provides what is referred to as “done for you sales” services to our clients. Think of a lead generation based marketing agency…. But focused on sales 🤪Put simply, our clients outsource their sales department to us and we sell their services/packages to help them scale faster than ever before while changing as many people’s lives as possible. The main verticals we service are in the online, digital marketing based community with companies that have educational programs that teach high paying skill sets which is referred to as “alternative education.” We sell a range of transformative programs and packages including everything from business consulting programs, to programs that teach people how to invest in real estate, learn mergers and acquisitions and many many more. The world is changing and so is the education space with college application and admission rates down significantly. Bespoke alternative education is a multi billion dollar a year industry and growing, and you can be a part of the gold rush. We believe people’s dream lives are just on the other side of receiving the right information- we’re responsible for getting that to them.

Competitive Comp Structure & Earning Potential!

Selling Life Changing Products!

Managing Top Performing Fully Remote Sales Teams!

Position Overview:

As an outsourced sales company, one of the main ways we differentiate ourselves is by positioning that we are not just “done for you sales” but rather “done for you sales operations.” The distinction is that while competitors just simply provide the sales talent, we bring a more comprehensive solution that includes sales management and all of our scaling systems. Needless to say, the Sales Director is a critical role in our sales management infrastructure, and in the overall solution we provide to our clients.. The way our management structure is designed is that each Sales Director oversees a few key accounts depending on the size, sales volume, and overall workload. This dynamic role varies in day to day responsibilities based on the specific demands of the assigned accounts and the critical areas of focus, but includes overseeing pipeline management, consistently conducting call reviews, evaluating rep performance, ensuring CRM data & reporting accuracy to make projections, identify training & rep development opportunities, and consistently suggesting operational improvements to maximize sales and find new levels of untapped potential for the prospective accounts.

You SHOULD apply to this role if:

  • You have experience managing sales teams in the high ticket alternative education space (Required)

  • You have extensive experience working in lead generation based businesses

  • You are great at managing the qualitative side of sales (culture, training, rep development) AND quantitative side of sales (data, sales metrics, performance KPIs, and quotas)

  • You have extensive experience driving efficiency through tech stack & a process to minimize revenue leakage

  • You understand the importance of sales enablement & can help ideate & give input on sales material

  • You know how to lead and motivate high intensity sales teams

  • Sales tech and spreadsheets don't stress you out

  • You understand the importance of establishing a feedback loop with marketing

  • You’ve had challenges finding your current role exciting

  • You’re stuck in a mundane repeatable process working in a static environment

  • You believe in the power of data and use it to make informed decisions

  • You enjoy fast paced energetic environments

  • You LOVE learning new things & having fun at the same time

You SHOULD NOT apply to this role if:

  • You are NOT an independent thinker

  • You don’t have real experience managing high ticket sales teams through data & forecasts

  • You haven’t managed a sales team with at least 5 or more sales reps

  • If you think it would be lame to help sales teams grow lightening fast

  • If you can’t learn CRM systems and manage through reports

  • You are absolutely clueless when it comes to understanding lead generation

  • You get frustrated easily instead of looking at challenges as a puzzle to solve

  • You are NOT teachable and do NOT seek personal development

  • You eat your pizza with ranch (may be flexible on this one)

Major Roles & Responsibilities:

  • Evaluates lead flow ratios and rep capacity on a daily basis

  • Works closely with marketing teams on lead flow initiatives to ensure profitable return on ad spend for our accounts

  • Tracks and monitors sales reps’ pipelines to ensure best lead management practices

  • Consistently managing out of the CRM to find and prevent missed opportunities

  • Run all daily sales syncs

  • Create sales trainings for sales training center (STC)

  • Enforce adherence to sales process SOPs

  • Reviews and analyzes calls recordings and creates call reviews for training purposes

  • Helps strategize deals with sales reps to increase sales

  • Maintains projections and manages sales quotas

  • Track and evaluate sales rep performance to make data driven decisions

  • Exemplify the Curvion Blue's core values & display rep spotlights

  • Review all end of day reports from sales reps

  • Attend all account status meetings

  • Study account offers/product knowledge (training center resident expert)

  • Communicate staffing needs based on capacity & performance

  • Assist the CSO & recruiting team in interviewing and hiring new sales reps

  • Onboarding, training, and ramping new sales reps

  • Work with the sales integrators on all data, reporting, & CRM accuracy

  • Takes complete revenue ownership

Role Type: Contractor

jobs.excerpt: About the roleWe are seeking a Senior Solutions Architect with deep security expertise to join the Voyager team in the Mirantis Office of the CTO.
jobs.description:
About the role

We are seeking a Senior Solutions Architect with deep security expertise to join the Voyager team in the Mirantis Office of the CTO. You will own the security solutioning of k0rdent AI, our platform for building and operating GPU clouds and AI factories, from metal to model.

You will define how k0rdent AI environments are secured end to end: the hardware and firmware they boot from, the hosts, virtual machines and Kubernetes clusters they run, the networks and storage they share, the secrets and certificates that hold them together, and the AI models and applications they serve. You will turn that design into published reference architectures, working code and proofs of concept that run on real hardware with our customers and partners.

As part of the Office of the CTO, research is a core part of the job. You will explore threats, designs and technologies before customers ask for them, prototype ideas that may not ship, and challenge established practice when a better approach exists. Your work will shape where k0rdent AI goes next, not only how it is deployed today.

This role combines research with hands-on, outward-facing work. You will split your time between exploring new designs, writing architecture, building and validating it in the lab, and explaining it to engineers, security teams, executives and conference audiences. You will work with Solutions Architects, Partner Management and Engineering colleagues across many countries and time zones.

Key Responsibilities

Reference architecture

  • Design and publish security reference architectures and solution designs for k0rdent AI, covering single-tenant private AI clouds, multi-tenant GPU clouds and hybrid deployments that span public cloud and on-premises infrastructure.

  • Define a defence-in-depth model across the stack, from hardware root of trust and firmware to hosts, virtual machines, Kubernetes, networks, storage, models and applications.

  • Define tenant isolation boundaries and their guarantees, and document where each boundary is strong, where it is weak, and what it costs to strengthen.

  • Map designs to the controls and frameworks customers must meet, and document trade-offs (risk, cost, performance, operability) with defensible reasoning a customer can follow.

Platform and infrastructure security

  • Bare-metal and host security: secure and measured boot, TPM-based attestation, BMC and Redfish hardening, firmware integrity, and hardened Linux hosts.

  • Virtual machine security: hypervisor and KubeVirt hardening, VM isolation, and the security implications of PCI passthrough and SR-IOV for GPUs and NICs.

  • Kubernetes security: RBAC, Pod Security Standards, admission control and policy-as-code, runtime security, and secure multi-cluster and multi-tenant operation.

  • Secrets management: secret stores, KMS and HSM integration, envelope encryption, secret delivery to workloads, and rotation.

  • Certificates and PKI: internal certificate authorities, automated issuance and rotation, mTLS between services, and workload identity.

  • Network security: segmentation and zero-trust designs, Kubernetes network policy, tenant isolation on front-end and GPU fabrics, and DPU-based security enforcement.

  • Storage security: encryption at rest and in transit, key management, and tenant isolation on shared block, file and object storage used for training data and model weights.

  • Public cloud security: secure landing zones, identity and access management, and network controls on major public clouds, and how they extend to hybrid deployments.

AI model and application security

  • Define how Transformer-based models are protected through their lifecycle: provenance and signing of model weights, integrity of training and fine-tuning data, and secure model registries.

  • Secure inference services and AI applications against threats such as prompt injection, data and model exfiltration, model theft and abuse of agentic tool access.

  • Design isolation for shared GPU infrastructure (MIG, vGPU, passthrough) and assess confidential computing options for protecting models and data in use.

  • Secure the software supply chain for platforms, containers and models: image signing, SBOMs, vulnerability management and provenance.

Research and exploration

  • Track and evaluate emerging security technologies, standards and threats, such as confidential computing on GPUs, remote attestation, post-quantum cryptography, model signing and AI agent security.

  • Prototype alternative designs in the lab, including ones customers have not yet asked for, and measure them against current practice.

  • Challenge established or customer-preferred designs when evidence points to a better option, and make the case with data.

  • Publish findings as internal research notes and design proposals and, where appropriate, as external papers, blog posts or talks.

Code and proofs of concept

  • Build and run proofs of concept with customers and partners, on Mirantis lab hardware and on customer sites, and report results against agreed success criteria.

  • Write automation, policies and tooling (Python, Go, Bash, Ansible, Helm, Kubernetes manifests, Terraform, policy-as-code) that make the reference architectures reproducible.

  • Assess designs and deployments through threat modelling, configuration review and hands-on testing, and turn findings into design guidance.

Customers, partners and community

  • Act as the security subject matter expert in customer discovery, design reviews and architecture workshops, bringing thought leadership and new ideas rather than only reflecting current practice.

  • Innovate and feed research results back to Product, Engineering and the Mirantis security team, and help shape the k0rdent AI roadmap.

  • Present at industry events, webinars and partner summits, and run hands-on workshops for technical audiences.

  • Write technical content: reference architecture documents, solution briefs, blog posts and internal enablement.

Location, travel and working model

This role is remote and based in the United States, with a strong preference for the East Coast.

  • You will work with a team spread across many time zones; some meetings will fall outside standard local hours.

  • Travel of up to 25% for customer engagements, partner meetings, lab work and industry events, primarily within the US and EU.

  • Mirantis is an equal opportunity employer. Compensation and benefits are set according to the local market and employment arrangement.

Qualifications

Education and experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Cybersecurity or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 8+ years in security engineering or security architecture, with at least 3 years securing cloud, Kubernetes or large-scale infrastructure platforms.

  • Customer-facing experience as a solutions architect, pre-sales engineer, consultant or technical lead.

Required technical skills

  • Cloud security: designing and operating secure deployments on at least one major public cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP) and on private cloud or bare-metal infrastructure.

  • Host and virtualisation security: Linux hardening (e.g. SELinux or AppArmor, CIS benchmarks), secure boot, TPM, and hypervisor and VM isolation, including KubeVirt.

  • Kubernetes security: RBAC, Pod Security Standards, admission controllers and policy engines (e.g. Kyverno, OPA Gatekeeper), runtime security (e.g. Falco), and multi-tenancy patterns.

  • Secrets and key management: tools such as HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao, External Secrets Operator, cloud KMS and HSMs.

  • PKI and identity: certificate lifecycle with tools such as cert-manager, mTLS, OIDC and SSO, and workload identity (e.g. SPIFFE/SPIRE).

  • Network security: segmentation, firewalling, zero-trust architectures and Kubernetes network policy (e.g. Cilium, Calico).

  • Storage and data security: encryption at rest and in transit, key hierarchy design, and access control on shared storage.

  • AI security: a working understanding of how Transformer-based models are trained, packaged and served, and the threats specific to them (e.g. OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, MITRE ATLAS).

  • Software supply chain security: image signing (e.g. Sigstore/cosign), SBOMs, vulnerability scanning and SLSA concepts.

  • Programming or scripting in at least one language (Python or Go preferred), and comfortable using Git, CI and infrastructure-as-code.

How you work

We hire for these behaviours as much as for technical depth, and will ask for concrete examples of each.

  • Curious. You dig into how attacks actually work, read the specs, advisories and source, and keep up with how AI and infrastructure threats are changing. You question established designs, including the ones customers are used to, when there is a better way.

  • Ownership. You take a reference architecture or a POC from the first sketch to a published, validated result, and you stand behind it.

  • Proactive. You spot risks and gaps in the product, the documentation or a customer design before you are asked, and you act on them.

  • Fast learner. You get productive quickly in unfamiliar hardware, software or customer environments.

  • Business acumen. You frame security decisions in terms of risk, cost, compliance and time-to-value, and explain them in those terms to decision makers.

Communication and collaboration

  • Excellent written and spoken English; you write documents others can build from.

  • Comfortable presenting to large audiences at conferences and events, and running hands-on workshops.

  • Able to adapt the message to the audience, from engineers to CISOs and customer executives.

  • Experience working in an international, distributed company, across time zones and different work cultures, with Solutions Architects, Partner Management and Engineering teams.

Nice to have

  • Experience with compliance frameworks and benchmarks relevant to cloud and AI infrastructure, such as NIST SP 800-53, NIST AI RMF, FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, CIS benchmarks or DISA STIGs.

  • Hands-on experience with confidential computing (e.g. AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, NVIDIA GPU confidential computing) and remote attestation.

  • Experience securing GPU cloud, neocloud or HPC environments, or NVIDIA Cloud Partner (NCP) style deployments.

  • Experience with DPUs (e.g. NVIDIA BlueField) for infrastructure isolation and security offload.

  • Offensive security or red-teaming experience, including against AI systems.

  • Experience with Mirantis products, MKE, k0s, k0rdent security.

  • Security certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, CKS, OSCP, or public cloud security specialty certifications.

  • Contributions to open-source security or Kubernetes projects, or a track record of public talks and technical writing.

  • Participation in standards or industry bodies (e.g. CNCF TAG Security, OpenSSF, Confidential Computing Consortium, CoSAI), or published research, CVEs, patents or white papers.

  • Additional languages beyond English.

Why you’ll love Mirantis

  • Collaborate with a world-class, distributed team committed to openness and technical excellence

jobs.excerpt: About Dynamo AIDynamo AI builds the platform enterprises use to bring AI applications to production and keep them there.
jobs.description:
About Dynamo AI

Dynamo AI builds the platform enterprises use to bring AI applications to production and keep them there. Our products cover risk assessment, evaluation, runtime guardrails and observability for generative AI and agentic systems. We work with enterprises in regulated industries, including financial services, insurance, healthcare and defense.

The Role

Every AI application needs policies that define acceptable behavior, and guardrails built and tuned against those policies. Legal, risk and compliance teams hold much of the knowledge those policies depend on. They have no prior experience or mandate to write policy definitions for guardrails or to annotate data, and there is usually no process that brings them into guardrail creation and optimization. They are also rarely the teams that buy our products, which are usually purchased by security and AI platform leaders.

As Product Manager for AI Governance & Compliance, you will design how these teams take part in policy writing, guardrail creation and guardrail optimization where no such process exists today. That means working out who needs to contribute, what they sign off on, and how their participation is secured through the economic buyer. It also means building the product workflows that make their contribution practical within the time they can give. This requires an understanding of how large enterprises assign responsibility and how teams outside the buying organization are brought into new work.

You will also support work on audit-ready evidence records and on turning regional regulations into enforceable guardrails. Picking up where our sales teams leave off, you will own the customer relationship and ensure a successful deployment of Samsara's solution. Your customers span the entire range of businesses that power our economy, including trucking and transportation, food and beverage, passenger transit, utilities, school buses, and many others. This role requires exceptional customer-facing communication skills, the ability to quickly understand a customer's business, and comfort explaining technology products to both executives and day-to-day users.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in Canada.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
  • You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
  • You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

In this role, you will:

  • Be on the front-lines and ensure our customers increase the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of their operations with our IoT platform
  • Manage the deployment of Samsara technology to Mid-Market customers, enabling customers to achieve quick time to value in their investment
  • Create launch plans and a roadmap to increase product usage
  • Track implementation progress, participation, product adoption, and account health
  • Run training sessions, demonstrate Samsara’s technology, and work through challenges with executives and day-to-day users of the system across numerous use cases
  • Juggle multiple customer engagements in parallel and work cross-functionally to deliver an exceptional experience for our customers
  • Deeply understand the Samsara platform’s capabilities and explain them to customers of all types
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 2-4+ years of experience in a senior Customer Success, account management, or strategic consulting role. Mid-Market SaaS experience preferred
  • English and French fluency
  • This is a demanding position with high internal visibility, that requires strong priority management and high emotional intelligence
  • Experience supporting or working with technical products
  • Excellent consultative skills with experience in end-to-end system implementations
  • Proven track record of building trust and communicating effectively with a wide variety of stakeholders: executives, Product and Engineering leadership, day-to-day users of our software
  • Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues

An ideal candidate also has:

$79,204.55—$102,500 USD

Total Rewards

jobs.excerpt: Company OverviewVenbrook Group, LLC is one of the fastest-growing independently owned insurance brokerage, claims, and risk management consulting companies in the United States.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Venbrook Group, LLC is one of the fastest-growing independently owned insurance brokerage, claims, and risk management consulting companies in the United States. Headquartered in Los Angeles, Venbrook operates across multiple U.S. locations through its subsidiaries, including retail brokerage, wholesale brokerage, specialty programs, and claims services. Our culture is approachable, adaptable, and entrepreneurial-spirited, with a commitment to diversity, inclusivity, and respect.


About The Role

Venbrook is seeking a Director, Claims Management & Excellence to lead claim handling and raise the standard for how our TPA claims operation works. Reporting to the Head of TPA Claims, this leader will evaluate claim processes end to end, find where workflow and technology can raise quality and efficiency, own claims quality assurance and performance KPIs, oversee a claims handling team, and help design new claims products we can take to market.

The role is both strategic and hands-on. The Director will set the direction for a new way of operating and build the processes, data, and tools behind it. They will also stay close enough to the work to understand a claim file, test a new workflow with the people who use it, and represent the operation with clients, carriers, and leadership.

The right candidate is a proven claims leader who has changed how a claims operation runs, not just managed one. They pair deep claims knowledge with sound business sense, a strong analytical mind, and a record of modernizing how work gets done.


What You'll Do

Claims process evaluation and strategy

  • Set the vision, roadmap, and annual goals for claims optimization so they support Venbrook's overall claims and business priorities.
  • Map and assess claim workflows end to end, from first notice of loss through intake, assignment, investigation, reserving, litigation management, recovery, payment, and closure.
  • Find bottlenecks, handoffs, rework, and leakage, and measure their effect on cycle time, cost, and claim outcomes.
  • Design future-state workflows, standard operating procedures, authority levels, and best practices across lines of business, including general liability, auto, property, and public entity.
  • Lead process improvement projects using Lean, Six Sigma, or similar methods, and track the benefits after rollout.

Claims team leadership and claim handling oversight

  • Lead a claims team, including claims supervisors, examiners, and oversee day-to-day claim handling against Venbrook and client quality and production standards.
  • Manage inventory, file assignments, caseloads, and service standards, including escalation and reassignment of files as needed.
  • Give technical direction on complex, high-exposure, or litigated claims, including coverage and liability analysis, reserving, resolution strategy, and settlement within assigned authority.
  • Review and approve reserves, payments, and settlements within authority, and present large-loss and roundtable reviews to clients and carriers.
  • Oversee defense counsel, independent adjusters, experts, and other vendors, including selection, performance, and cost control.
  • Make sure claim handling follows client service instructions, fair claims practices rules, and applicable state regulations.
  • Use the team as a pilot group to test new workflows, tools, and quality standards before rolling them out more widely.

Technology modernization and automation

  • Build and own the claims technology roadmap with the Head of TPA Claims, IT, and corporate operations.
  • Evaluate, choose, and roll out claims systems, workflow tools, and insurtech partners, including AI, document intake automation, robotic process automation, predictive analytics, and client reporting portals.
  • Act as business owner for system changes: write requirements, set priorities, run user acceptance testing, and drive adoption.
  • Partner with data teams on data quality and on models that flag severity, litigation risk, fraud, and recovery opportunities earlier.
  • Make sure new tools meet Venbrook's data privacy, security, and AI governance standards.

Quality assurance and compliance

  • Build and lead the claims quality assurance program, including file review standards, audit sampling, scoring, calibration, and feedback to claims managers and staff.
  • Prepare the operation for client, carrier, and regulatory audits, and lead remediation when findings arise.
  • Monitor compliance with fair claims practices rules, client service instructions, reserving guidelines, and authority levels.
  • Turn quality findings into training, process fixes, and system controls.

Performance management and KPIs

  • Set and track key performance indicators such as cycle time, closure rate, pending inventory and age, caseload, reserve accuracy, indemnity and expense leakage, litigation rate, recovery dollars, contact timeliness, and client satisfaction.
  • Build reporting and dashboards that give leadership, claims managers, and clients clear, timely views of performance, and lead monthly operating reviews.
  • Benchmark results against industry standards and client service agreements, and set improvement targets.
  • Use data to support staffing models, capacity planning, and caseload balance.

Product development and client growth

  • Partner with the Head of TPA Claims, sales, and business development to design new claims products and services, such as technology-enabled or tiered service models, analytics and risk insight offerings, and program or captive claims support.
  • Assess market need, competitor offerings, pricing inputs, and operating requirements for new offerings, and build the business case for leadership.
  • Support client proposals, finalist presentations, and client onboarding with operating design, KPIs, and technology capabilities.
  • Represent Venbrook's claims capabilities with clients, carriers, brokers, and in industry settings.

People leadership and change management

  • Lead, mentor, and develop claims professionals, analysts, and quality assurance specialists, and direct cross-functional project teams. Set clear expectations, conduct performance reviews, and handle performance issues promptly and fairly.
  • Lead change management, including communication, training, and coaching, so new ways of working take hold.
  • Create training programs that strengthen technical skills and spread best practices across claims teams.
  • Manage project timelines, budgets, and vendor relationships.

Cross-functional partnership

  • Work with claims, IT, legal, finance, and client-facing teams to build optimization into every stage of the claim lifecycle.
  • Work with finance on the cost and return of process and technology investments.
  • Escalate significant matters to the Head of TPA Claims and executive leadership with clear, well-supported recommendations.

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree required. CPCU strongly preferred. MBA or other relevant industry designations (such as AIC, ARM, AIM, AIS, SCLA, or CRM) are preferred.
  • 10 or more years of property and casualty claims experience across several lines of business, including hands-on claims handling and claims operations.
  • 5 or more years of progressive leadership experience in claims operations, including managing claims supervisors and examiners, plus experience in operational excellence or process improvement, ideally in a TPA, carrier, or self-insured setting.
  • A record of redesigning claims processes or operating models, with measurable gains in quality, cycle time, cost, or client results.
  • Experience leading technology or process modernization, such as claims system implementations, analytics, automation, or AI tools.
  • Experience building quality assurance programs and KPI frameworks, and turning data into decisions.
  • Experience designing or launching new products, services, or service models, and supporting business development and client retention.
  • Deep knowledge of claims best practices, reserving, litigation management, fair claims practices rules, and multi-state regulatory requirements.
  • Lean Six Sigma, project management (PMP), or business intelligence tool experience (such as Power BI or Tableau) is a plus.
  • Strong business sense, including experience with budgets, vendor spend, business cases, and financial reporting.
  • Excellent communication, change leadership, and executive presence, with the ability to influence clients, partners, and senior leadership.

Compensation

The anticipated base salary range for this position is $95,000 - $130,000. Actual compensation will depend on factors including location, relevant experience, and qualifications.

Overview

Nelson Mullins, an AmLaw 100 firm, is seeking an Intellectual Property Litigation Docketing Specialist. The IP Litigation Docketing Specialist will be a member of the Litigation Docketing Department and works under the supervision of the Litigation Docketing Manager. The IP Litigation Docketing Specialist will collaborate closely with attorneys and legal staff to provide thorough and accurate intellectual property litigation calendaring services for all federal, state, and agency matters, including ITC. Responsibilities include reviewing court documents, legal correspondence, and case team requests and entering deadlines into the firm’s rules-based calendaring software, Milana. The IP Litigation Docketing Specialist will follow all firm docketing procedures, best practices, and workflows. The IP Specialist will assist in the department’s mission of delivering best in class service to clients and mitigating risk to the firm.

This position is open to a fully remote schedule for the right candidate.

A Day in the Life

The responsibilities for this role include independently reviewing patent, trademark, trade secrets, and copyright litigation court documents and legal correspondence, and accurately entering deadlines into the firm’s rules-based calendaring software, Milana. The candidate must ensure compliance with all department procedures, best practices, and workflows, and respond to requests from attorneys and legal staff regarding deadlines and court rules. Conducting jurisdictional research and providing comprehensive summaries to case teams, with oversight from the senior docketing staff and Manager as needed, is essential. The candidate must ensure assigned calendaring is accurate and completed in a timely manner and provide back-up litigation docketing services for the Houston and Dallas centralized inboxes.
